app.name: Conbert
app.subtitle: FileWizard
app.intro: Convert files into other formats or make them smaller – right on your device or on your own server.

server.checkingHelp: Conbert is checking whether your server can be reached.
server.onlineHelp: Your Conbert server is reachable. Conversions on the server are possible.
server.offlineHelp: Your Conbert server isn't responding right now. Conversions on this device still work.
server.degradedHelp: Your server is reachable, but its job queue (Valkey) isn't running. Server conversions aren't possible right now – this device still works.

dropzone.label: Add files
dropzone.title: Drag files here
dropzone.hint: Or click here to choose files. Whole folders and pasting with Ctrl+V work too.

files.mismatch: Note: the file ends in “.{{nameExt}}” but is actually a {{format}}. Conbert handles it correctly.

convert.noTargets: There's no conversion for this file type (yet).
convert.gotBigger: The new file is bigger than the original. That's normal when you convert e.g. a JPG into a lossless format like PNG.
convert.noCommonTargets: There's no format all files can be converted to. Choose the target for each file instead.
convert.downloadAllHelp: Downloads every finished file at once. Several files are packed into one ZIP file – open it with a double click, Windows and macOS handle it without extra software. Files with the same name get a number.
convert.zipFailed: The ZIP file couldn't be created. Download the files one by one.

libvips.description: A fast specialist for photos and images. Converts between JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF, TIFF and JPEG XL – right in your browser.

sharp.description: A fast image specialist on your server. Converts JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF and TIFF – even large photos in seconds.

imagemagick.description: The all-rounder for images on your server. Also knows rare formats like BMP, ICO, TGA, Photoshop files and iPhone photos (HEIC).

ffmpegAudio.description: The expert for music and sound on your server. Converts between MP3, M4A, FLAC, WAV, Ogg, Opus and more.

ffmpegVideo.description: The expert for videos on your server. Converts between MP4, WebM, MKV, MOV and more, makes GIFs and extracts the sound – using the graphics card if there is one.

pandoc.description: The translator for text documents: converts between Word, LibreOffice, Markdown, HTML, e-book and many other text formats – keeping the structure.

vtracer.description: Traces pictures into vector graphics (SVG). Ideal for logos, icons and drawings that should stay sharp at any size.

magickWasm.description: The all-rounder for images, right in your browser. Also knows BMP, ICO, TGA, JPEG 2000, Photoshop files and iPhone photos (HEIC) – and works without HTTPS too.

ffmpegWasm.description: Converts music and videos right in your browser – the files never leave your device. For large videos the server is much faster.

mediabunny.description: The fast one for videos and music in your browser: it uses your browser's built-in codecs (often sped up by the graphics card). If the content already fits the target format, it is only repackaged – no quality loss, done in seconds. If your browser can't handle something, FFmpeg takes over automatically.

spessasynthMidi.description: Plays MIDI files with real instrument sounds and records them as a music file – right in your browser. MIDI files only contain notes, no sound; the sounds come from the bundled "GeneralUser GS" soundfont (loaded once the first time, about 32 MB).

spessasynthSoundfont.description: Converts soundfonts (instrument collections for MIDI) between SF2, SF3 and DLS – right in your browser. SF3 can be read but not written.

pandocWasm.description: Converts texts and documents (Word, OpenDocument, Markdown, HTML, e-book …) – right in your browser, the files never leave your device. About 58 MB are loaded the first time, after that it's quick.

gbaVideo.description: Turns a video into a cartridge for the Game Boy Advance. The picture is shrunk to the small GBA screen and reduced to 256 colours, the sound is stored as simple retro audio. Buttons on the device: START/A = pause, ◀/▶ = 10 seconds back/forward, L/R = 1 minute back/forward, B = from the start, SELECT = endless playback on/off.

assimp.description: The read-anything for 3D models on your server: opens over 40 formats (FBX, Collada, 3DS, X3D …) and saves the common ones.

gltfTransform.description: Specialist for glTF/GLB: makes 3D models smaller (packing shapes, shrinking textures, reducing detail) without visible difference.

three3d.description: Converts 3D models right in your browser (OBJ, STL, PLY, glTF/GLB, FBX, DAE, 3DS, 3MF). Saves as GLB, glTF, OBJ, STL, PLY or USDZ.

libreofficeWriter.description: LibreOffice for text documents on your server: convert Word (DOC/DOCX), OpenDocument and RTF and save as PDF – with a faithful layout.

libreofficeCalc.description: LibreOffice for spreadsheets on your server: convert Excel (XLS/XLSX), OpenDocument and CSV and save as PDF.

libreofficeImpress.description: LibreOffice for presentations on your server: convert PowerPoint (PPT/PPTX) and OpenDocument and save as PDF.

pdfTools.description: Ghostscript and qpdf on your server: shrink PDFs (with or without quality loss) and save single pages as pictures.

pdfjsRender.description: Renders PDF pages right in your browser and saves a page as a picture (PNG or JPG).

calibre.description: Calibre on your server – the e-book specialist: EPUB, Kindle (MOBI, AZW3), FictionBook and PDF. Only included in the "full" edition of Conbert.

archives.description: Repacks archives (ZIP, 7Z, TAR, TAR.GZ, also opens RAR) – on your server, protected against dangerous paths and huge "archive bombs".

archivesWasm.description: Repacks archives right in your browser: opens ZIP, 7Z, RAR, TAR and TAR.GZ and saves as ZIP, TAR or TAR.GZ.

fonttools.description: fonttools on your server: convert fonts between TTF, OTF, WOFF and WOFF2 and shrink them to the characters you need.

dataFormats.description: Converts data and tables: JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, CSV and Excel (XLSX) – in the browser or on the server.

ocrmypdf.description: Text recognition (OCR) for scanned PDFs: afterwards you can search the document and copy text. Runs on the server only.

whisper.description: Speech recognition: turns spoken sound (also from videos) into subtitles or plain text. Runs on the server only.

imageAi.description: Artificial intelligence for pictures on the server: remove the background (ISNet) and upscale (Real-ESRGAN). Used via “Enhance” in the picture card.

blender.description: The free 3D program Blender, running invisibly on your server: opens Blender files, USD and Alembic and saves them e.g. as GLB, OBJ or STL. Has to be installed once under Administration.

subtitles.description: Converts subtitles: SRT, WebVTT and ASS into each other or into plain text – in the browser or on the server.

subtitleExtract.description: Takes subtitles out of videos: the built-in subtitles (e.g. from MKV) or – if there are none – from the spoken words via speech recognition. Runs on the server only.

svgo.description: Makes SVG graphics smaller: removes what is not needed (comments, editor notes, repeated values) and shortens numbers. The graphic looks the same afterwards.

quality.label: Quality
quality.help: How much detail is kept. 80 is a good middle ground: you'll barely see a difference, but the file is much smaller.
quality.effect: Higher = nicer image, but bigger file. Lower = smaller file, but maybe visible blocks or blur.

lossless.label: Lossless
lossless.help: Stores the image exactly, pixel by pixel, without leaving out any detail. The quality slider is ignored then.
lossless.effect: On: a perfect copy, but usually a much bigger file. Good for graphics and screenshots.

effort.label: Effort
effort.help: How much time Conbert takes to get the file as small as possible. The image quality stays the same.
effort.fastHelp: Done in a moment, the file ends up a bit bigger.
effort.balancedHelp: A good compromise between time and file size. Right for almost everything.
effort.smallHelp: Takes noticeably longer, but squeezes out a few more percent.

stripMetadata.label: Remove metadata
stripMetadata.help: Removes hidden extra info like the date taken, camera model and above all the GPS location where a photo was taken. Color information is kept.
stripMetadata.effect: On (recommended): protects your privacy and saves a few kilobytes. Off: all info stays in the file.

keepAnimation.label: Keep animation
keepAnimation.help: For animated images (e.g. GIF) all frames are kept. Off: only the first frame is saved.

pngPalette.label: Color palette (smaller PNG)
pngPalette.help: Reduces the image to at most 256 colors, similar to GIF. For logos and graphics you often can't see a difference.
pngPalette.effect: On: the file often gets 2–4× smaller. For photos, color gradients may look blotchy.

tiffCompression.label: TIFF compression
tiffCompression.help: How the TIFF file is packed. “Deflate” and “LZW” are lossless and readable by almost every program.
tiffCompression.jpegHelp: Uses the quality slider. Smaller, but no longer lossless – usually unsuitable for print.

audioQuality.label: Sound quality
audioQuality.help: How good the sound should be. “Balanced” is almost always right for music and speech.
audioQuality.effect: Better = bigger file. Smaller = the file shrinks; with music you'll hear it at some point (duller, “tinny”).
audioQuality.highHelp: Hard to tell apart from the original. Good for music you listen to often.
audioQuality.balancedHelp: Sounds good and saves a lot of space. Right for almost everything.
audioQuality.smallHelp: Fine for speech, audiobooks and podcasts. Noticeably worse for music.

audioBitrate.label: Bitrate (sound)
audioBitrate.help: How much data per second is stored for the sound, in kilobits per second (kbit/s). “Automatic” takes the value from the sound quality.
audioBitrate.effect: Higher = better sound, bigger file. 128 kbit/s sounds good to most people, 192–320 for music lovers.

sampleRate.label: Sample rate
sampleRate.help: How often per second the sound is measured, in hertz. 44,100 Hz is CD quality, 48,000 Hz the standard for videos. “Like original” is usually right.

channels.label: Channels
channels.help: Stereo has separate sound for left and right, mono just one channel.
channels.monoHelp: Halves the size of uncompressed sound. Good for voice recordings.

loudness.label: Even out loudness
loudness.help: Makes quiet recordings louder and loud ones quieter, the way your ears hear it (measured to EBU R128). Handy when several songs or episodes should sound equally loud.
loudness.effect: The result sounds evenly loud. Very quiet parts are lifted a little, loud ones softened a little. Converting takes a bit longer.
loudness.offHelp: The loudness stays as it is.
loudness.musicHelp: As loud as on Spotify or YouTube. Good for music and videos to watch.
loudness.speechHelp: A little calmer, good for podcasts, audiobooks and voice recordings.
loudness.broadcastHelp: The European standard for broadcasters. Sounds much quieter than music apps – only pick it when it is required.

trimSilence.label: Remove silence at the start and end
trimSilence.help: Cuts off silent parts before the first and after the last sound, e.g. the wait after pressing "record". Pauses in the middle stay.
trimSilence.effect: The file gets a little shorter. Very quiet hiss counts as silence; a short rest (0.1 seconds) stays so the sound doesn't start abruptly.

videoQuality.label: Video quality
videoQuality.help: How sharp and detailed the video should stay. “Balanced” looks good on phones and TVs.
videoQuality.effect: Better = bigger file. Smaller = the file shrinks a lot; fast movement may show blocks.
videoQuality.highHelp: Almost no difference from the original. For memories and archives.
videoQuality.balancedHelp: Looks good and saves a lot of space. Right for almost everything.
videoQuality.smallHelp: For sending when it has to be small. A little blurrier.

resolution.label: Resolution
resolution.help: How many pixels high the video is. Conbert never enlarges – small videos stay as they are. GIFs are reduced to at most 480 pixels unless you choose otherwise, because GIFs get huge.
resolution.effect: Smaller = much smaller file, less sharp on big screens.

fps.label: Frames per second
fps.help: How many single pictures are shown per second. Fewer frames = smaller file, but movement looks choppier. For GIFs, 12 frames are used unless you choose otherwise.

videoCodec.label: Video codec
videoCodec.help: The “packing method” for the picture. The codec decides how small the file gets and which devices can play it.
videoCodec.autoHelp: H.264 for MP4/MOV/MKV, VP9 for WebM – plays almost everywhere.
videoCodec.h264Help: Plays on practically every device. The safe choice.
videoCodec.h265Help: About half the size of H.264 at the same quality. Newer devices, iPhone, TVs.
videoCodec.av1Help: Very modern and smallest. Needs current devices and takes longer.
videoCodec.vp9Help: Google's free codec, standard for WebM and YouTube.

encoderSpeed.label: Speed
encoderSpeed.help: How much time Conbert takes. More time means a smaller file at the same quality.

removeAudio.label: Remove sound
removeAudio.help: The video is saved without a sound track, e.g. for background videos on websites.

useGpu.label: Use graphics card
useGpu.help: If your server has a suitable graphics card, it often converts videos 3–10× faster than the processor.
useGpu.effect: On: much faster, the file gets a bit bigger at the same quality. Off: slower, but smallest. If the graphics card doesn't work out, Conbert automatically continues without it.

tableOfContents.label: Table of contents
tableOfContents.help: Adds a table of contents made from all headings at the beginning.

markdownFlavor.label: Markdown variant
markdownFlavor.help: There are several “dialects” of Markdown. Most programs understand the GitHub variant.
markdownFlavor.gfmHelp: With tables and task lists. Works in GitHub, Obsidian, VS Code and many wikis.
markdownFlavor.commonmarkHelp: The standardized basic version – very compatible, but without tables.
markdownFlavor.markdownHelp: With many extras like footnotes. Best if you'll work with Pandoc again later.

colorMode.label: Colors
colorMode.help: Whether the vector graphic is colorful or only black and white.
colorMode.colorHelp: Keeps the picture's colors. For logos and illustrations.
colorMode.bwHelp: Only black outlines. Good for signatures, stamps and line drawings.

vectorDetail.label: Detail
vectorDetail.help: How closely the picture is traced. For logos, “Balanced” is usually ideal; for photos and illustrations, “Lots of detail” or “Maximum”.
vectorDetail.effect: More detail = more accurate, but a bigger SVG with many small shapes. Less = smoother and smaller, fine details disappear.
vectorDetail.maxHelp: Keeps even the tiniest specks and finest color shades. The SVG can get very big and slow down programs that open it.
vectorDetail.highHelp: Very accurate but still manageable. Good for illustrations and detailed logos.
vectorDetail.balancedHelp: A good middle ground between accuracy and file size. Fits most logos.
vectorDetail.smallHelp: Smooth shapes, small file. Small details are dropped.
vectorDetail.minHelp: Only the big shapes in a few colors – like a screen-printed poster. Very small file.

curveMode.label: Line style
curveMode.splineHelp: Round, smooth lines – looks best for most logos.
curveMode.polygonHelp: Only straight lines. Good for pixel graphics and angular shapes.
curveMode.noneHelp: Follows every pixel. For pixel art.

gbaQuality.label: Sharpness or length
gbaQuality.help: A GBA module holds at most 32 MB. The sharper the picture, the more space each second takes – and the shorter the video may be.
gbaQuality.effect: “Sharp” looks best but only fits short clips. “Longer” is a bit more pixelated, but several minutes fit on the module.
gbaQuality.sharpHelp: 240 × 160 pixels, exactly the GBA screen. Good for short clips: roughly 1–3 minutes.
gbaQuality.balancedHelp: 160 × 104 pixels, enlarged to the full screen by the GBA. Roughly 3–8 minutes.
gbaQuality.longHelp: 120 × 80 pixels, doubled in size, and slightly simpler sound. Roughly 6–14 minutes.

gbaFps.label: Frames per second
gbaFps.help: How often per second the picture changes. Fewer frames save space, but movement looks choppier.
gbaFps.effect: Higher = smoother, but shorter videos fit on the module. Lower = longer videos, choppier.

gbaSound.help: The module is built without sound. That saves a lot of space – much longer videos fit.

gbaLoop.label: Play endlessly
gbaLoop.help: At the end the video starts again by itself – e.g. as a continuous loop. On the Game Boy you can switch this on and off at any time with SELECT.

modelBinary.label: Save as binary
modelBinary.help: Binary is smaller and loads faster. As text you can read the file in an editor – but only developers need that.

meshCompression.label: Pack shapes
meshCompression.help: Shrinks the data of the 3D shape (points and triangles) – often by 50–90 %.
meshCompression.effect: Meshopt is lossless and loads fast. Draco is even smaller but changes the shape minimally and loads a bit slower.
meshCompression.noneHelp: Most compatible: every program can open the file.
meshCompression.meshoptHelp: Lossless and fast. Works in browsers, three.js, Babylon.js and Godot.
meshCompression.dracoHelp: Smallest, minimally less precise. Runs on the server. Supported by most viewers.

textureFormat.label: Textures
textureFormat.help: Textures are the pictures on the model – often the biggest part of the file. As WebP they get much smaller.
textureFormat.webpHelp: Much smaller with hardly visible difference. Very old programs may not load WebP textures.

textureSize.label: Textures at most
textureSize.help: Very large textures are reduced to this edge length. For phones and the web 1024 or 2048 pixels are usually enough.

simplify.label: Reduce detail
simplify.help: Removes triangles where you hardly see it – good for very detailed scans.
simplify.effect: Fewer triangles = smaller file and smoother display, but curves get more angular.

pdfQuality.label: Shrink PDF
pdfQuality.help: Pictures are usually the biggest part of a PDF. The more they are reduced, the smaller the file.
pdfQuality.effect: Stronger = smaller file, but pictures get blurrier. Text always stays sharp.
pdfQuality.losslessHelp: Only tidies up and packs better – nothing gets worse. Often saves 5–30 %.
pdfQuality.printerHelp: Pictures stay sharp enough for printing.
pdfQuality.ebookHelp: Good for reading on screen and sending. The best choice in most cases.
pdfQuality.screenHelp: Pictures get noticeably blurrier – only for a quick look.

pdfPage.label: Page
pdfPage.help: Which page of the PDF is saved as a picture (1 = first page).

pdfDpi.label: Resolution
pdfDpi.help: How many pixels per inch. 150 is enough for screens, 300 for print.

fontSubset.label: Characters to keep
fontSubset.help: Fonts often contain thousands of characters (e.g. Greek, Cyrillic). If you only need German or English, the rest can be left out.
fontSubset.effect: Fewer characters = much smaller file. Missing characters will later show in a fallback font.
fontSubset.latin-extHelp: Latin script incl. special letters (e.g. Polish, Czech, Turkish).
fontSubset.latinHelp: A–Z, umlauts, ß and common punctuation – smallest.

archiveLevel.label: Packing
archiveLevel.help: How much the files in the archive are squeezed together.
archiveLevel.effect: Stronger = smaller archive but takes longer. Photos and videos hardly shrink because they are already packed.
archiveLevel.normalHelp: Good balance of size and speed.

csvDelimiter.label: Separator
csvDelimiter.help: What separates the columns in the CSV file. Excel in Germany expects a semicolon.
csvDelimiter.semicolonHelp: For Excel in Germany, Austria, Switzerland.
csvDelimiter.commaHelp: Common internationally, e.g. for programs and English Excel.
csvDelimiter.tabHelp: Good when texts themselves contain commas and semicolons.

jsonIndent.label: Indent for readability
jsonIndent.help: With indentation the file is easy to read, without it is a bit smaller.

epubTitlePage.label: Title page
epubTitlePage.help: Adds a page with the title at the start of the e-book. Conbert uses the document's own title (e.g. from Word's file properties) – if it has none, the file name.

vectorTraceSize.label: Trace at
vectorTraceSize.help: The size the picture is traced at. The finished SVG can always be scaled freely – but the more pixels during tracing, the finer the outlines.
vectorTraceSize.effect: Bigger = finer, rounder outlines, but slower and a bigger file. Smaller = faster, rougher.
vectorTraceSize.fastHelp: Big pictures are scaled down to 1024 pixels. For a quick preview.
vectorTraceSize.normalHelp: Big pictures are scaled down to 2048 pixels, small ones stay as they are.
vectorTraceSize.fineHelp: Small pictures (e.g. a 200-pixel logo) are enlarged to 2048 pixels first. Curves become smooth instead of stair-stepped.
vectorTraceSize.maxHelp: Traces at 4096 pixels and enlarges small pictures. The finest result, but it can take a few minutes.

vectorLayers.label: Layers
vectorLayers.help: How the colored shapes are arranged in the SVG.
vectorLayers.stackedHelp: Shapes lie on top of each other like paper cut-outs. No gaps between colors – usually the best choice.
vectorLayers.cutoutHelp: Each shape has holes where other colors are. Handy if you want to edit parts separately later or cut them with a plotter or laser.

vectorSpeckle.label: Small specks
vectorSpeckle.help: From what size small color specks are kept. Dropping them cleans up noise and dust.
vectorSpeckle.effect: Finer = even tiny dots stay (more accurate, bigger file). Coarser = small specks disappear (cleaner).

vectorColorPrecision.label: Color accuracy
vectorColorPrecision.help: How precisely colors are told apart. With low accuracy, very similar shades become one color.
vectorColorPrecision.effect: Finer = more different colors (more natural, bigger file). Coarser = fewer colors (flatter, like a comic).

vectorGradientStep.label: Color gradients
vectorGradientStep.help: How finely gradients (e.g. a sky from light to dark) are split into separate shapes.
vectorGradientStep.effect: Finer = many thin bands, the gradient looks soft. Coarser = a few wide steps, visible edges.

vectorCorners.label: Corners
vectorCorners.help: From what bend an outline gets a sharp corner instead of a curve.
vectorCorners.effect: Finer = more sharp corners, follows the picture more closely. Coarser = more curves, looks softer.

vectorSegmentLength.label: Curve pieces
vectorSegmentLength.help: How long the pieces are that a curve is built from.
vectorSegmentLength.effect: Finer = short pieces that follow every small bulge (more points, bigger file). Coarser = long, smooth curves.

vectorSplice.label: Split curves
vectorSplice.help: From what change of direction a curve is split into two.
vectorSplice.effect: Finer = more curve parts, more accurate shapes. Coarser = fewer but smoother curves.

vectorPathPrecision.label: Coordinate accuracy
vectorPathPrecision.help: How many decimal places the points in the SVG are saved with.
vectorPathPrecision.effect: Finer = more exact points, bigger file. Coarser = smaller file; with very coarse values, edges may wobble slightly.

ocrLanguage.label: Language of the text
ocrLanguage.help: The language the document is written in. With the right language, Conbert recognises special letters and words much more reliably. For mixed documents choose “German and English”.

ocrRotate.label: Turn pages the right way up
ocrRotate.help: Finds pages that are upside down or were scanned sideways and turns them so they can be read.

ocrDeskew.label: Straighten crooked pages
ocrDeskew.help: Straightens pages that were scanned or photographed at a slight angle. This helps the text recognition.
ocrDeskew.effect: On: tidier pages and better text, but the page is saved again as a picture (slightly bigger file).

ocrMode.label: Pages that already have text
ocrMode.help: Many PDFs already contain real text (e.g. from Word). Choose what happens to such pages.
ocrMode.skipHelp: Only pages without text are recognised. Fast, and existing text stays untouched.
ocrMode.redoHelp: For PDFs with poor, old text recognition: the old invisible text layer is replaced, the look stays.
ocrMode.forceHelp: Every page is turned into a picture and recognised again. Last resort for broken PDFs – real text and links are lost.

speechLanguage.label: Spoken language
speechLanguage.help: The language that is spoken. “Detect automatically” usually works – if the result is nonsense or in the wrong language, set the language yourself.

translateToEnglish.label: Translate into English
translateToEnglish.help: Writes the text in English right away, whatever language is spoken. Handy for English subtitles to a video in another language.

subtitleShift.label: Shift time (seconds)
subtitleShift.help: Moves all subtitles earlier or later. Helps when the text doesn’t match the picture, e.g. because the subtitles belong to another version of the film.
subtitleShift.effect: Plus = subtitles appear later, minus = earlier. Example: if the text comes 2 seconds too early, enter 2.

subtitleSource.label: Where do the subtitles come from?
subtitleSource.help: Many videos (MKV above all) already have subtitles built in – Conbert can take them out directly. Otherwise speech recognition can write them from the spoken words.
subtitleSource.autoHelp: Built-in subtitles if the video has any – otherwise speech recognition.
subtitleSource.trackHelp: Only the built-in subtitles. If the video has none, you get a note.
subtitleSource.speechHelp: Writes the subtitles anew from the spoken words – even if the video already has some (takes longer).

subtitleTrack.label: Subtitle track
subtitleTrack.help: If the video has several subtitles (e.g. German and English), choose which one here: 1 = the first, 2 = the second and so on. Your video player shows the order (e.g. VLC under “Subtitle”).

burnSubtitles.label: Burn subtitles into the picture
burnSubtitles.help: Paints the video’s built-in subtitles right into the picture. Then they show everywhere – also on TVs, phones and websites that can’t display subtitles.
burnSubtitles.effect: On: subtitles always visible, but they can’t be switched off any more. The video is re-encoded for this (takes longer).

burnSubtitleTrack.label: Which subtitle track to burn in
burnSubtitleTrack.help: If the video has several subtitles (e.g. German and English), choose which one goes into the picture: 1 = the first, 2 = the second and so on. Your video player shows the order (e.g. VLC under “Subtitle”).

burnSubtitleFile.label: Burn in your own subtitle file
burnSubtitleFile.help: Choose an SRT, VTT or ASS file to be written into the picture – e.g. subtitles you downloaded for the film or made with speech recognition. Takes precedence over “Burn subtitles into the picture”.

svgPrecision.label: Precision
svgPrecision.help: How many decimal places the coordinates keep. Fewer places = smaller file. You will not see “Balanced” on normal graphics.
svgPrecision.effect: Less precision makes the file smaller, but fine lines and small icons can move slightly.
svgPrecision.small: As small as possible (can get inexact)

svgKeepEditorData.label: Keep editor data
svgKeepEditorData.help: Inkscape, Illustrator & co. store layer names, notes and their own details in the SVG. Only the drawing program needs them. On = they stay (to keep editing), off = they are removed (smaller).

engineStatus.uninitializedHelp: This engine loads automatically the first time you need it.
engineStatus.loadingHelp: The engine is being downloaded and started. This only happens the first time.
engineStatus.readyHelp: The engine is loaded and can start right away.
engineStatus.partialHelp: The engine works, but some formats are missing because an add-on module couldn't be loaded. Reload the page to try again.
engineStatus.errorHelp: The engine can't be used right now. When converting you'll see why and what you can do.

local.label: On this device
local.help: Your files stay on your computer. Most private, but slower for large videos.

server.label: On the server
server.help: The file is sent to your own server and converted there. Faster and more formats.

auto.label: Automatic
auto.help: Conbert picks what fits best for you – and tells you why.

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Choose how Conbert looks and works. Settings are stored in your account and apply on all your devices.

engines.title: Engines
engines.intro: Engines are the specialists that convert your files. The ones in the browser are only loaded when you need them.
engines.noServer: Your server doesn't report any engines of its own yet. Server conversions arrive with the next update.

theme.label: Color scheme
theme.help: Light, dark, or whatever your operating system is set to.

language.label: Language
language.help: The language Conbert talks to you in. “Automatic” uses your browser's language.

magicEffects.label: Magic effects
magicEffects.help: A little sparkle when something is done, and playful loading texts. Always off if your system is set to “reduce motion”.

defaultMode.label: Default for new files
defaultMode.help: Where new files are converted. You can change this for each file.

expertMode.label: Expert mode
expertMode.help: Shows every option. Without expert mode you only see what matters most: target format and quality.
expertMode.effect: On: more options, for people who know what they're doing. Off: tidy, and the results are still good.

threshold.label: Convert on the server above this size
threshold.help: In “Automatic” mode, files larger than this are converted on your server instead of this device.
threshold.effect: Lower value: spares your device. Higher value: more stays on your device, but large files take longer.

gpu.label: Graphics card
gpu.found: Graphics card found ({{gpu}}): your server often converts videos 3–10× faster with it.
gpu.none: No usable graphics card found – videos are converted with the processor. That works too, it just takes longer.
gpu.help: On start, Conbert checks with a small test conversion whether a graphics card can speed up videos. In Docker, the graphics card has to be passed through to the container: Intel and AMD via “/dev/dri”, NVIDIA via the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Examples are in docker-compose.yml as comments.

offline.title: Use offline
offline.intro: Conbert can keep itself in the browser so “On this device” also works without internet or while the server is off. Tools you use are stored automatically – here you can load all of them at once.
offline.unavailable: Offline use only works when you open Conbert over HTTPS or http://localhost (and not in a private window). With an address like http://192.168.1.20:3313 the browser doesn't allow it.
offline.complete: Everything stored ({{size}}). Conbert also works offline on this device.
offline.partial: {{cached}} of {{total}} stored. What's missing is loaded on first use – or all at once now.

error.what: Not all files could be stored.
error.cause: The connection dropped or the browser is out of space.
error.action: Try again. If that doesn't help, free up storage in the browser settings.

booruEnabled.label: Show booru area
booruEnabled.help: Booru sites are image collections, often with anime and drawn art. Turn this on if you want to download images from them – the Booru tab, its settings and booru subscriptions then appear. Turning it off only hides everything; existing subscriptions keep running.

jpg.name: JPEG image
jpg.summary: The best-known format for photos. Saves a lot of space but loses a little quality.
jpg.badFor: Logos, graphics with text and anything with a transparent background

png.name: PNG image
png.summary: Stores images without any quality loss and supports transparent areas.
png.goodFor: Logos, screenshots, graphics with text, images with transparency
png.badFor: Large photos – the file gets very big very quickly

webp.name: WebP image
webp.summary: Modern image format by Google: smaller than JPG, supports transparency and animation.
webp.goodFor: Websites, saving space, images with transparency
webp.badFor: Very old programs that don't know WebP yet
webp.openWith: All current browsers, Windows 10/11, macOS, Android, iPhone

avif.name: AVIF image
avif.summary: A very modern image format with especially small files at good quality.
avif.goodFor: Websites, saving as much space as possible
avif.badFor: Older devices and programs – AVIF isn't supported everywhere yet

gif.name: GIF image
gif.summary: Old format for small animations. Can only show 256 colors at once.
gif.badFor: Photos – the colors will look blotchy

tiff.name: TIFF image
tiff.summary: Professional format for print and archiving. Lossless, but the files are large.
tiff.goodFor: Print shops, scans, archiving, image editing
tiff.badFor: Websites and sending to others – far too big
tiff.openWith: Image editors, Windows Photos, macOS Preview

jxl.name: JPEG XL image
jxl.summary: New successor to JPG: smaller files, better quality, lossless is possible too.
jxl.goodFor: Archiving photos, saving space at high quality
jxl.badFor: Sending to others – many devices and browsers can't open JPEG XL yet
jxl.openWith: Safari, Windows 11 (with extension), newer image programs

svg.name: SVG vector graphic
svg.summary: A graphic made of lines and shapes instead of pixels. Stays sharp at any size.
svg.badFor: Photos – they can't be described sensibly as lines

heic.name: HEIC photo
heic.summary: The photo format of iPhones. Saves a lot of space, but isn't shown everywhere.
heic.badFor: Sending to Windows or Android users – better convert to JPG

bmp.name: BMP image
bmp.summary: A very old Windows format without compression. Files get huge.
bmp.goodFor: Old programs and devices that know nothing else
bmp.badFor: Almost everything else – PNG is just as lossless but much smaller
bmp.openWith: Every Windows program, most image viewers

ico.name: ICO icon
ico.summary: Format for small icons, e.g. the little picture in the browser tab (favicon).

tga.name: TGA image
tga.summary: An older format from games and graphics, lossless and with transparency.

psd.name: Photoshop file
psd.summary: Adobe Photoshop working file with layers. Conbert uses the finished, combined picture.
psd.goodFor: Editing further in Photoshop, GIMP or Affinity
psd.badFor: Viewing without an image editor – better convert to PNG or JPG

jp2.name: JPEG 2000 image
jp2.summary: JPG's successor from the year 2000; rare in everyday use, but popular in archives and medicine.
jp2.badFor: Websites – most browsers can't show it

mp3.name: MP3 audio
mp3.summary: The best-known music format. Small and plays everywhere.
mp3.goodFor: Music, podcasts, audiobooks, phone and car
mp3.badFor: Archiving in top quality – better FLAC

wav.name: WAV audio
wav.summary: Uncompressed sound in full quality. Files are very large.
wav.goodFor: Audio editing, music production, further processing
wav.badFor: Sending and storing many songs – far too big

flac.name: FLAC audio
flac.summary: Losslessly compressed sound: full quality, but only about half the size of WAV.
flac.goodFor: Music archive, hi-fi systems, backing up CDs
flac.badFor: Older devices and iPhones without a suitable app
flac.openWith: VLC, Android, Windows 10/11, most hi-fi players

ogg.name: Ogg Vorbis audio
ogg.summary: A free, lossy audio format – similar to MP3, often a little better.
ogg.badFor: Apple devices – they often don't play Ogg

opus.name: Opus audio
opus.summary: A very modern audio format: sounds good even at small sizes, especially for speech.

m4a.name: M4A audio (AAC)
m4a.summary: Apple's audio format: sounds better than MP3 at the same size.
m4a.goodFor: iPhone, iTunes, Apple Music, phones in general

aac.name: AAC audio
aac.summary: Raw AAC sound without a container – technically like M4A, but rarer as a file.
aac.badFor: Everyday use – M4A is more common

aiff.name: AIFF audio
aiff.summary: Uncompressed sound, Apple's counterpart to WAV.
aiff.goodFor: Music production on the Mac, Logic, GarageBand
aiff.badFor: Sending to others – very large files

wma.name: WMA audio
wma.summary: An old Microsoft audio format, rarely used today.
wma.badFor: Phones and Apple devices – better convert to MP3

mp4.name: MP4 video
mp4.summary: The standard video format: plays practically everywhere.
mp4.badFor: Hardly anything – when in doubt, MP4 is the right choice

webm.name: WebM video
webm.summary: A free video format for the web, often smaller than MP4.

mkv.name: MKV video
mkv.summary: A flexible “video container” for films with several audio tracks and subtitles.
mkv.goodFor: Archiving films, several languages and subtitles
mkv.badFor: Phones and browsers – they often can't play MKV
mkv.openWith: VLC, Kodi, Plex, many smart TVs

mov.name: MOV video
mov.summary: Apple's video format, e.g. from iPhone cameras.
mov.goodFor: Apple devices, editing with Final Cut
mov.badFor: Windows users without a suitable player – better MP4

avi.name: AVI video
avi.summary: A very old video format from Windows days.
avi.badFor: Phones, websites, modern use – better MP4

wmv.name: WMV video
wmv.badFor: Phones, Macs and websites – better MP4

mpg.name: MPEG video
mpg.summary: An old video format as used on video CDs and DVDs.
mpg.badFor: Modern devices – the files are large

mid.name: MIDI file
mid.summary: Not a recording but “sheet music” for the computer: which instruments play which notes when.
mid.badFor: Just listening – sounds different on every device, better convert to MP3
mid.openWith: MuseScore, DAWs like FL Studio, some players

sf2.name: SoundFont 2
sf2.summary: A collection of instrument sounds used to play MIDI files.
sf2.badFor: Listening to music – it's not a recording

sf3.name: SoundFont 3
sf3.summary: Like SoundFont 2, but with compressed sounds – much smaller files.
sf3.badFor: Older programs that only know SF2

dls.name: DLS sound bank
dls.summary: An older format for instrument sounds, mainly used by Windows and Apple.

md.name: Markdown text
md.summary: Plain text with small marks for formatting, e.g. **bold** or # heading.
md.badFor: Letters and designed documents – better DOCX
md.openWith: Any text editor, Obsidian, Typora, VS Code

html.name: HTML page
html.summary: The format of web pages – opens in the browser.
html.goodFor: Websites, e-mails, viewing in the browser
html.badFor: Printing with a fixed layout – better PDF or DOCX

docx.name: Word document
docx.summary: Microsoft Word's text format, the standard in offices.
docx.badFor: Publishing with a fixed look – better PDF

odt.name: OpenDocument text
odt.summary: LibreOffice's free text format – the open counterpart to Word.
odt.badFor: People who only use Word – it may look slightly different there

rtf.name: RTF document
rtf.summary: An old, simple format for formatted text that almost every program can read.
rtf.badFor: Modern documents with images and tables

txt.name: Plain text
txt.goodFor: Notes, further processing, when only the content matters
txt.openWith: Any text editor on any device

rst.name: reStructuredText
rst.summary: Text with formatting marks, similar to Markdown, popular in Python projects.

tex.name: LaTeX document
tex.summary: A typesetting format for scientific work with formulas.
tex.badFor: Quick everyday documents – takes some learning

org.name: Org mode text
org.summary: Text with formatting marks from the Emacs editor – for notes, tasks and outlines.
org.goodFor: Notes and to-do lists in Emacs
org.badFor: Sharing with people who don't use Emacs

epub.name: EPUB e-book
epub.summary: The standard format for e-books: text adapts to the screen size.

gba.name: GBA module (Game Boy Advance)
gba.summary: A Game Boy Advance cartridge image that plays your video – with a small built-in video player.
gba.goodFor: Watching videos on a Game Boy Advance (via a flash cart) or in an emulator, retro fun
gba.badFor: Long videos – a module holds at most 32 MB. Picture and sound are “retro” (few colours, small screen).
gba.openWith: Game Boy Advance with a flash cart (e.g. EverDrive, EZ-Flash), emulators such as mGBA

pdf.name: PDF document
pdf.summary: A document that looks the same everywhere – on every device and when printed.
pdf.badFor: Editing later – Word or OpenDocument are better for that
pdf.openWith: Any browser, Adobe Acrobat Reader, Preview (Mac)

glb.name: GLB (glTF binary)
glb.summary: Modern 3D format in a single file: model, colours and textures together.
glb.goodFor: Websites, game engines, AR, sharing 3D models
glb.badFor: 3D printing – STL or 3MF are better for that
glb.openWith: Windows 3D Viewer, Blender, browser viewers, Godot, Unity

gltf.name: glTF (text)
gltf.summary: Like GLB, but as a readable text file. Conbert embeds everything so it stays a single file.
gltf.goodFor: Developers who want to look at or edit the model in a text editor

obj.name: OBJ model
obj.summary: Ancient, very widespread 3D format – almost every program can open it.
obj.badFor: Animations and materials (Conbert saves the shape only)
obj.openWith: Blender, Windows 3D Viewer, almost every 3D program

stl.name: STL (3D printing)
stl.summary: The standard format for 3D printers: just the shape, no colours.
stl.goodFor: 3D printing, slicers like Cura or PrusaSlicer
stl.openWith: Cura, PrusaSlicer, Bambu Studio, Windows 3D Viewer

ply.name: PLY model
ply.summary: 3D format from research, often used for 3D scans and point clouds.
ply.goodFor: 3D scans, point clouds, models with per-point colours
ply.badFor: Games and web – GLB is better

fbx.name: FBX model
fbx.summary: Widespread format from the film and games industry (by Autodesk).
fbx.badFor: Open, long-lasting archives – GLB is better

dae.name: Collada (DAE)
dae.summary: Older open 3D exchange format based on XML.

3ds.name: 3DS model
3ds.summary: Very old format from 3D Studio – some programs still need it.
3ds.badFor: Large, detailed models (it has fixed size limits)

3mf.name: 3MF (3D printing)
3mf.summary: Modern 3D printing format, the successor of STL – also knows colours and units.
3mf.openWith: PrusaSlicer, Cura, Bambu Studio, Windows 3D Builder

x3d.name: X3D model
x3d.summary: Open 3D standard for the web, successor of VRML.

usdz.name: USDZ (Apple AR)
usdz.summary: Apple's 3D format for augmented reality on iPhone and iPad.
usdz.goodFor: AR view on iPhone/iPad, Quick Look
usdz.openWith: iPhone, iPad, Mac (Quick Look), Reality Composer

doc.name: Word document (old)
doc.summary: The old Word format up to Office 2003.

pptx.name: PowerPoint presentation
pptx.badFor: Sending to be viewed – PDF is better
pptx.openWith: PowerPoint, LibreOffice Impress, Google Slides, Keynote

ppt.name: PowerPoint (old)
ppt.summary: The old PowerPoint format up to Office 2003.

odp.name: OpenDocument presentation
odp.badFor: Exchange with PowerPoint users – PPTX is better

xlsx.name: Excel spreadsheet
xlsx.summary: Spreadsheet from Microsoft Excel with numbers, formulas and several sheets.
xlsx.badFor: Simple data exchange with programs – CSV is better
xlsx.openWith: Excel, LibreOffice Calc, Google Sheets, Numbers

xls.name: Excel spreadsheet (old)
xls.summary: The old Excel format up to Office 2003.

ods.name: OpenDocument spreadsheet
ods.badFor: Exchange with Excel users – XLSX is better

csv.name: CSV table
csv.summary: Simple table as text: one line per record, columns separated by a character.

json.name: JSON data
json.summary: Structured data as text – the standard format for websites and programs.
json.badFor: People who want to read tables – XLSX is better
json.openWith: Text editor, browser, any code editor

yaml.name: YAML data
yaml.summary: Structured data as easily readable text, often for settings.

toml.name: TOML data
toml.badFor: Large amounts of data and tables

xml.name: XML data
xml.summary: Structured data with tags, like HTML – older but very widespread.
xml.goodFor: Older interfaces, data exchange between companies

mobi.name: Kindle book (MOBI)
mobi.summary: Older e-book format of the Amazon Kindle.
mobi.badFor: New devices – AZW3 or EPUB are better

azw3.name: Kindle book (AZW3)
azw3.summary: Current e-book format for the Amazon Kindle.
azw3.badFor: Other e-readers (Tolino, Kobo) – EPUB is better

fb2.name: FictionBook (FB2)
fb2.summary: Open e-book format, common mainly in Eastern Europe.

zip.name: ZIP archive
zip.summary: Several files packed into one – the most widespread archive format.
zip.openWith: Windows, macOS, Linux, phones – built in everywhere

7z.name: 7-Zip archive
7z.summary: Archive format with very strong compression.
7z.goodFor: Saving space, archiving large amounts of data

tar.name: TAR archive
tar.summary: Bundles files without shrinking them – common on Linux.
tar.goodFor: Linux servers, backups (often packed on top)
tar.badFor: Saving space – TAR.GZ or 7Z are better

tgz.name: TAR.GZ archive
tgz.summary: TAR archive additionally shrunk with gzip – standard on Linux.
tgz.badFor: Windows users without extra software – ZIP is better

rar.name: RAR archive
rar.summary: Widespread archive format from WinRAR. Conbert can open and repack it, but not create it.
rar.goodFor: Opening and repacking into ZIP or 7Z
rar.badFor: New archives – RAR is not freely available

ttf.name: TrueType font
ttf.summary: Font file that can be installed on any computer.

otf.name: OpenType font
otf.summary: Modern font file with many typographic extras.

woff.name: WOFF web font
woff.badFor: Installing on a computer – TTF/OTF are better

woff2.name: WOFF2 web font
woff2.summary: The smallest font file for websites – about 30 % smaller than WOFF.
woff2.badFor: Installing on a computer – TTF/OTF are better

srt.name: SRT subtitles
srt.summary: The best-known subtitle file: text with times when it appears.
srt.goodFor: Subtitles for video players (VLC, Plex, Jellyfin), YouTube uploads
srt.openWith: Any text editor; video players load it when it has the same name as the video
srt.badFor: Styling such as colours or position (use ASS for that)

vtt.name: WebVTT subtitles
vtt.summary: Subtitle format for the web – like SRT, but made for browsers.
vtt.goodFor: Videos on websites (HTML5 players), online courses
vtt.openWith: Any text editor, browser video players
vtt.badFor: Older TVs and video players that only know SRT

blend.name: Blender file
blend.summary: Blender's working file – holds the models, materials, lights and camera of a whole scene.
blend.badFor: Sharing with people without Blender – GLB is better

usd.name: USD scene
usd.summary: Pixar's “Universal Scene Description”: an open format for whole 3D scenes that many programs exchange.
usd.goodFor: Exchange between Blender, Houdini, Maya, Omniverse
usd.badFor: Web and phones – GLB or USDZ is better

usdc.name: USD scene (binary)
usdc.summary: The compact, binary version of USD – loads faster than USDA.
usdc.badFor: Reading or editing by hand – use USDA for that

usda.name: USD scene (text)
usda.summary: USD as readable text – good for checking and for small scenes.
usda.goodFor: Checking scenes or adjusting them by hand
usda.badFor: Large scenes – the file quickly gets huge

abc.name: Alembic cache
abc.summary: Stores moving 3D geometry frame by frame – e.g. simulations of cloth, water or smoke.
abc.goodFor: Animations and simulations between film and effects programs
abc.badFor: Single models with materials – GLB or FBX is better

ass.name: ASS subtitles
ass.summary: Subtitles with styling: font, colours, position and effects (also as .ssa).
ass.goodFor: Anime and fan subtitles, karaoke, subtitles with colours or at certain places in the picture
ass.badFor: TVs and simple players that only know SRT
ass.openWith: VLC, mpv, Jellyfin, Plex; edit with Aegisub

warnings.transparencyLost: Heads up: this format has no transparency. Transparent areas will turn white.
warnings.animationLost: Heads up: this format can't animate. Only the first frame is kept.
warnings.lossy: This format saves space by leaving out details. The quality may drop a little.
warnings.onlyAudio: Only the sound is taken from the video – the picture is dropped.
warnings.formattingLost: Plain text has no formatting: bold text, headings, images and tables are lost.

reasons.modeLocal: Converted on this device, as you set it up.
reasons.modeServer: Converted on your server, as you set it up.
reasons.autoBrowser: Automatic: the file is converted on this device – that's the most private option.
reasons.autoFileTooLarge: Automatic: the file is larger than {{threshold}}, so your server takes over.
reasons.autoServerOnly: Automatic: only your server can do this conversion.
reasons.autoGpuVideo: Automatic: your server has a graphics card and converts videos much faster.
reasons.onlyOnServer: This conversion only works on the server. Switch the mode to “On the server” or “Automatic”.
reasons.onlyInBrowser: This conversion only works on this device. Switch the mode to “On this device” or “Automatic”.
reasons.serverUnavailable: Your server can't be reached right now.
reasons.noRoute: Sorry, there is no way (yet) to do this conversion.

warnings.largeFileLocal: Large file: on this device this may take a while and use a lot of memory.

routing.chain: Not possible directly, but in {{count}} steps: {{path}}

engineLoadFailed.what: The conversion engine couldn't be loaded.
engineLoadFailed.cause: The connection dropped or your browser is too old for WebAssembly.
engineLoadFailed.action: Reload the page. If that doesn't help, choose “On the server” or use a current browser.

notIsolated.what: Converting on this device isn't possible here.
notIsolated.cause: Your browser only allows fast conversion over a secure connection (HTTPS) or via “localhost”. You are probably opening Conbert through a network address like http://192.168.…
notIsolated.action: Choose “On the server”, open Conbert via https:// (e.g. behind a reverse proxy) or directly on the server via http://localhost.

convertFailed.cause: The file is damaged or uses a variant of the format the engine doesn't know.
convertFailed.action: Try another target format or convert the file on the server.

outOfMemory.what: There isn't enough browser memory for this file.
outOfMemory.cause: The file is too big to convert on this device.
outOfMemory.action: Choose “On the server”, or close other tabs and try again.

formatUnavailable.what: This format isn't available right now.
formatUnavailable.cause: An add-on module of the engine couldn't be loaded.
formatUnavailable.action: Reload the page or choose another target format.

noRoute.what: There's no way to do this conversion right now.
noRoute.cause: No suitable engine is available in the chosen mode (“On this device”, “On the server” or “Automatic”).
noRoute.action: Switch the mode to “Automatic” or choose another target format.

network.cause: The server is switched off, restarting, or your device isn't on the same network.
network.action: Check that Conbert is running (e.g. with “docker compose ps”) and try again.

badResponse.what: The server sent an unexpected answer.
badResponse.cause: Browser and server are probably running different versions.
badResponse.action: Reload the page. If that doesn't help, restart the server.

notFound.what: What you were looking for wasn't found.
notFound.cause: The address is wrong or the item has been deleted in the meantime.
notFound.action: Go back to the start page and try again.

badRequest.what: The server couldn't process the request.
badRequest.cause: Invalid or incomplete information was sent.
badRequest.action: Reload the page and try again.

internal.what: An unexpected error happened on the server.
internal.cause: This is most likely a bug in Conbert, not something you did.
internal.action: Try again in a moment. If it happens again, check the server log.

unauthorized.cause: Your session expired or you signed out.

forbidden.what: You're not allowed to do this.
forbidden.cause: This feature is for administrators only.
forbidden.action: Ask the person who manages Conbert.

setupRequired.what: Conbert hasn't been set up yet.
setupRequired.cause: On first start, an administrator account must be created.
setupRequired.action: Reload the page – the setup will appear.

setupDone.cause: Someone has already created the administrator account.

invalidSetupCode.cause: The code was mistyped or is from an earlier start.
invalidSetupCode.action: Look up the current code in the server log, e.g. with “docker compose logs conbert”.

invalidLogin.cause: User name or password is wrong.
invalidLogin.action: Check what you typed (passwords are case-sensitive) and try again.

usernameTaken.cause: Each user name can only be used once.

weakPassword.action: Use a longer password – a sentence of several words is secure and easy to remember.

wrongPassword.cause: To change it, you must enter your existing password correctly.

lastAdmin.what: The last administrator can't be removed.
lastAdmin.cause: Without an administrator, nobody could manage accounts anymore.
lastAdmin.action: Make another account an administrator first.

crossOrigin.what: The request was blocked for security reasons.
crossOrigin.cause: It came from a different website than Conbert.
crossOrigin.action: Open Conbert directly via its address and try again there.

fileTooLarge.what: The file is too large for the server.
fileTooLarge.cause: Your server only accepts files up to a certain size.
fileTooLarge.action: Convert the file on this device or ask the admin to raise CONBERT_MAX_UPLOAD_MB.

queueUnavailable.what: The job queue on the server can't be reached.
queueUnavailable.cause: The “Valkey” service that manages jobs isn't running.
queueUnavailable.action: Restart Conbert with “docker compose up -d” or convert on this device.

noServerRoute.what: The server can't do this conversion.
noServerRoute.cause: No suitable engine is installed on the server.
noServerRoute.action: Choose another target format or convert on this device.

resultGone.what: The result is no longer available.
resultGone.cause: Finished files are deleted automatically after a while to save space.

tooManyAttempts.cause: To protect against password guessing, signing in is blocked for a while after several failed attempts.

invalidUsername.what: This user name can't be used.
invalidUsername.cause: User names need 2 to 32 characters and may only contain letters without accents, digits and . _ -

proxyLoginMissing.cause: Conbert is set up so that your reverse proxy (e.g. Authelia or Authentik) handles sign-in – but it didn't send a user.
proxyLoginMissing.action: Open Conbert via your proxy's address. If that doesn't work, the admin should check CONBERT_AUTH_PROXY_HEADER and CONBERT_TRUSTED_PROXIES.

noMatchingStream.what: The file doesn't contain what you want.
noMatchingStream.cause: For example, the video has no sound track that could become an MP3.
noMatchingStream.action: Check the file (e.g. in VLC) or choose another target format.

allSilent.cause: The recording is empty or so quiet that no sound was found. "Remove silence" would leave nothing.
allSilent.action: Listen to the file. If it has sound, switch off "Remove silence at the start and end".

gbaTooLong.what: The video is too long for a GBA module.
gbaTooLong.cause: A Game Boy Advance module holds at most 32 MB. With these settings the module would be bigger.
gbaTooLong.action: Choose “Longer” under “Sharpness or length”, set fewer frames per second (expert mode) or shorten the video.

previewUnavailable.cause: Your browser can't show this format directly and converting it for the preview failed – or the file is damaged.
previewUnavailable.action: Converting often works anyway. Give it a try or open the file with another program.

noWebgl.cause: Your browser or graphics card doesn't support WebGL 2 (or it is switched off).
noWebgl.action: Converting still works. For the preview try a current browser such as Chrome, Edge or Firefox.

dataNotTable.what: This data can't be shown as a table.
dataNotTable.cause: CSV and Excel need a list of similar entries (e.g. [{"name": …}, {"name": …}]). This file is structured differently.
dataNotTable.action: Convert it to JSON, YAML, TOML or XML – they can store any structure.

dataInvalid.cause: It contains a mistake, e.g. a missing comma or wrong indentation.
dataInvalid.action: Check the file in a text editor – "Show details" tells you where the mistake is.

archiveTooLarge.what: The archive is too big to unpack.
archiveTooLarge.cause: Unpacked it would be huge or contains an extreme number of files – this can also be a deliberate "archive bomb".
archiveTooLarge.action: Unpack it with a program on your computer if you trust the source.

encrypted.what: The file is protected with a password.
encrypted.cause: Conbert can't open protected archives, PDFs or documents.
encrypted.action: Remove the password protection in the original program and try again.

storageAuth.what: Signing in to the storage location didn't work.
storageAuth.cause: User name, password or key are wrong – or the user may not open this folder.
storageAuth.action: Check user name and password. For Nextcloud, best use an app password.

storageUnreachable.cause: The device is off, not in the same network, or the address or port is wrong. A firewall can also block the connection.
storageUnreachable.action: Is the device on? Is the address right? If Conbert runs in Docker, the server must be able to reach the device – not just your PC.

storageNotFound.what: This folder or file doesn't exist there.
storageNotFound.cause: The name of the share, bucket or folder is misspelled, or it was deleted or renamed.
storageNotFound.action: Check the address and the folder. Upper and lower case can matter.

storageCertificate.cause: The device uses a certificate Conbert doesn't trust – often a self-made certificate of a NAS.
storageCertificate.action: Use the right address (with the name in the certificate). For FTPS, you can turn on “Don't check the certificate” in expert mode if you trust the device.

storageDenied.cause: The user may not read or write in this folder, or the folder is read-only.
storageDenied.action: Give the user write access to this folder on the NAS or server, or pick another folder.

storageFailed.what: Something went wrong while using the storage location.
storageFailed.cause: The storage location reported an unexpected error.
storageFailed.action: Try again. “Show details” tells you exactly what the storage location reported.

storageSecretLost.what: The stored password can't be read anymore.
storageSecretLost.cause: The key Conbert encrypts passwords with (CONBERT_SECRET) was changed.
storageSecretLost.action: Open the storage location in the settings and enter the password again.

storageTypeUnsupported.what: This kind of storage location isn't available (yet).
storageTypeUnsupported.cause: Cloud services with sign-in (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox) come later.

storageFieldMissing.cause: A required field is empty (SFTP needs a password or a key).
storageFieldMissing.action: Fill in all fields marked with *.

storageAddressInvalid.cause: Network folders need device and share (e.g. \\192.168.1.10\Photos), WebDAV and S3 an address starting with http:// or https://.
storageAddressInvalid.action: Best copy the address straight from Explorer, Finder or the Nextcloud settings.

storageRootNotAllowed.cause: Conbert may only use folders mounted into the container and allowed in CONBERT_STORAGE_ROOTS (default: /storage).
storageRootNotAllowed.action: Mount the folder under /storage in docker-compose.yml and restart Conbert.

storagePathInvalid.cause: The path leads out of the storage location's folder (e.g. with “..” or a shortcut).
storagePathInvalid.action: Pick a folder inside the storage location.

storageNotTarget.what: Saving to this storage location isn't allowed.
storageNotTarget.cause: It is only set up as a source to open files from.
storageNotTarget.action: Allow “Save results here” in the storage location's settings.

storageNotSource.what: Opening files from this storage location isn't allowed.
storageNotSource.cause: It is only set up as a target to save to.
storageNotSource.action: Allow “Open files from here” in the storage location's settings.

storageIsFolder.what: That's a folder, not a file.
storageIsFolder.cause: Only single files can be opened.
storageIsFolder.action: Open the folder and pick the files in it.

storagePreviewTooLarge.what: This file is too big for a preview.
storagePreviewTooLarge.cause: A preview would have to load the whole file – for files this big, that takes too long.
storagePreviewTooLarge.action: Just open the file; then you can look at it in Conbert.

metadataReadFailed.cause: The file may be damaged, or the reading tool couldn't be loaded.
metadataReadFailed.action: Reload the page and try again. Converting still works.

metadataWriteFailed.cause: The target format doesn't allow these details, or the converted file is built in an unusual way.
metadataWriteFailed.action: The converted file is ready anyway – just without your changes. Try another target format (e.g. JPG or MP4).

downloadUrlInvalid.what: That's not a link Conbert can load.
downloadUrlInvalid.cause: Only links starting with http:// or https:// that point to a public site are allowed – no addresses in your home network.
downloadUrlInvalid.action: Copy the link straight from the address bar or via “Share → Copy link”.

downloadPrivateAddress.what: This link leads into your home network.
downloadPrivateAddress.cause: The site’s name points to a device in your own network, for example your router or your NAS. Conbert doesn’t load anything from there, so nobody can use the downloader to reach devices behind your firewall.
downloadPrivateAddress.action: Check that the link is right. Files from your own network can be opened with “Open from storage”.

downloadHostUnknown.cause: The site’s name doesn’t exist (any more), is misspelled, or your server isn’t connected to the internet right now.
downloadHostUnknown.action: Check the spelling of the link and try opening it in your browser. If that works, try again in a few minutes.

downloadUnsupported.cause: Neither yt-dlp nor gallery-dl can load content from this site – or the link doesn't point to a video, picture or profile.
downloadUnsupported.action: Check the link. If that doesn't help, updating the tools in the settings may.

downloadLoginRequired.cause: The content is private, age-restricted or only visible to signed-in users.
downloadLoginRequired.action: Add your cookies for this site in the settings under “Download” (with a guide).

downloadNotFound.cause: The post was deleted, is private or isn't available in your country.
downloadNotFound.action: Open the link in your browser and check if it still works there.

downloadRateLimited.what: The site doesn't allow more requests right now.
downloadRateLimited.cause: Too much was loaded in a short time – the site slows down to protect itself.
downloadRateLimited.action: Wait a while and try again. Set a longer pause between requests in the settings.

downloadNothing.cause: The period or selection matches no post, or the content is only visible when signed in.
downloadNothing.action: Change period or selection, or add your cookies for this site.

downloadFailed.cause: The site reported an unexpected error – often it has changed.
downloadFailed.action: Try again. If that doesn't help, update the tools in the settings.

downloadToolMissing.cause: yt-dlp or gallery-dl isn't installed on this server (the Docker image has both).
downloadToolMissing.action: Use the Conbert Docker image or install yt-dlp and gallery-dl.

downloadUpdateFailed.cause: The server can't reach the internet, or the package source was unavailable.
downloadUpdateFailed.action: Check the server's internet connection and try again later.

downloadCookiesInvalid.cause: Conbert expects the “Netscape” format that extensions like “Get cookies.txt LOCALLY” create.
downloadCookiesInvalid.action: Export the cookies again, following the guide exactly.

downloadBlocked.what: The site blocks requests from your server.
downloadBlocked.cause: The site doesn't let programs like yt-dlp from your internet connection (IP address) reach its data right now – this has nothing to do with your account or cookies. Reddit currently does this for thread links.
downloadBlocked.action: Try again later or update the tools in the settings. The direct link to the video file usually works anyway (in the browser: right-click the video → “Copy video address”).

booruSiteUnknown.cause: The site was removed or the link is wrong.
booruSiteUnknown.action: Pick a site from the list or add it as your own instance.

booruQueryRefused.cause: At least one of the search terms is blocked in Conbert.

booruAuth.cause: Username (on Gelbooru: user ID) or API key are wrong, or your account may not see this.
booruAuth.action: Check username and API key in the settings.

booruUserIdInvalid.what: Gelbooru needs your user ID, not your name.
booruUserIdInvalid.cause: Gelbooru signs you in with a number (the user ID), not with your username.
booruUserIdInvalid.action: On Gelbooru, open “My Account → Options” and copy the whole line with “&api_key=…&user_id=…” into the “API key” field.

booruAccountsUnsupported.what: You can't add an account for this site.
booruAccountsUnsupported.cause: The site doesn't offer sign-in with an API key.
booruAccountsUnsupported.action: Use the site without an account.

booruNeedsAccount.what: This site only answers with an account.
booruNeedsAccount.cause: Gelbooru now only answers requests with a username and API key.
booruNeedsAccount.action: Create a free Gelbooru account and enter its user ID and API key in the settings.

booruRateLimited.what: The site wants Conbert to ask more slowly.
booruRateLimited.cause: Too many requests in a short time.
booruRateLimited.action: Wait a few minutes or use the slow mode.

booruBlocked.what: The site blocks requests from your server.
booruBlocked.cause: The site shows a security check (e.g. Cloudflare) instead of data. Conbert doesn't get around such blocks.
booruBlocked.action: Try again later or use another site.

booruTagLimit.what: Too many search terms for this site.
booruTagLimit.cause: Your account allows only a few tags per search, and these terms can only be checked by the site itself.
booruTagLimit.action: Remove terms like pool: or fav:, or use an account with more tags.

booruPageLimit.what: The site doesn't allow going further.
booruPageLimit.cause: Without an account, paging stops at a certain page number.
booruPageLimit.action: Sort by “Newest” (Conbert then pages by post ID) or use the slow mode.

booruUnreachable.cause: No internet connection, the site is offline or the address is wrong.
booruUnreachable.action: Check the connection and try again later.

booruFailed.action: Try again later. See “Show details” for more.

booruInstanceInvalid.cause: Only normal web addresses (http/https) are allowed; home-network addresses only if the admin enabled them.

booruAgeRequired.what: You need to confirm that you are an adult for this.
booruAgeRequired.cause: Adult content is only visible after the age confirmation.
booruAgeRequired.action: Confirm your age in the booru settings.

booruPinWrong.cause: The rating choice is locked with a PIN.

booruNothing.cause: No results, all hidden, or already downloaded.
booruNothing.action: Change the search or the filters.

booruJobNotActive.what: This job is not running anymore.
booruJobNotActive.cause: It is already finished or was cancelled.
booruJobNotActive.action: Start a new job if needed.

workflowStepUnavailable.cause: The step needs a tool that is missing (for now) – e.g. workshop tricks or ExifTool.
workflowStepUnavailable.action: Remove the step or try again after an update.

workflowImportInvalid.what: This file is not a Conbert workflow.
workflowImportInvalid.cause: The file is damaged or comes from another program.
workflowImportInvalid.action: Export the workflow again in Conbert and import that file.

workflowSaveFailed.cause: The storage location couldn't be reached or refused saving.
workflowSaveFailed.action: Check the storage location in the settings and run the workflow again.

notifyAddressInvalid.cause: Only normal web addresses are allowed; home-network servers only for admins, Discord only with a discord.com webhook address.

notifyFieldMissing.cause: This kind of notification needs more fields.

notifyFailed.cause: The service refused the message or can't be reached – often a wrong token or address.
notifyFailed.action: Check the details. See “Show details” for more.

feedIntervalTooShort.what: You can't look that often here.
feedIntervalTooShort.cause: Instagram blocks accounts that fetch profiles too often.

feedNotSubscribable.what: This link can't be subscribed to.
feedNotSubscribable.cause: A single video or picture never gets new content.
feedNotSubscribable.action: Subscribe to the profile, channel, playlist or thread – and simply download single items.

keyInvalid.what: This is no valid public key.
keyInvalid.action: Create the key again in the settings.

keyNotLocked.what: The private key isn't locked with a password.
keyNotLocked.cause: Conbert only stores private keys locked – so nobody on the server can read them.
keyNotLocked.action: Reload the page and create the key again.

keyNoRecipients.cause: No recipient is chosen in the step, you don't have a key yet, or the chosen users no longer share their key.
keyNoRecipients.action: Choose at least one recipient in the workflow or create your key in the settings.

mediaNoDefault.what: There is no default storage location.
mediaNoDefault.cause: The swipe game shows the pictures of your default storage location – none is marked as default yet.
mediaNoDefault.action: Open Settings → Storage locations and tick “Default” for one of them.

mediaSyncRunning.cause: Conbert is reading your storage location right now.
mediaSyncRunning.action: Wait a moment – the page shows when it is done.

mediaAlreadySwiped.cause: A decision for it is already waiting (it can be undone).
mediaAlreadySwiped.action: Take the decision back with “Back” if you want to change it.

downloadPixivLogin.what: Pixiv needs your account to be connected.
downloadPixivLogin.cause: Pixiv only shows works to logged-in users. Either no Pixiv account is connected yet, or Pixiv ended the connection (e.g. after a password change).
downloadPixivLogin.action: Connect your Pixiv account in the settings under “Download” (with a guide).

pixivCodeInvalid.what: That is not a Pixiv code.
pixivCodeInvalid.cause: The field doesn’t contain the address “pixiv://…code=…”, or only part of it.
pixivCodeInvalid.action: Copy the whole message with “code=” from the console and paste it again.

pixivCodeExpired.cause: A Pixiv code only lasts 30 seconds after logging in, and works only once.
pixivCodeExpired.action: Open the Pixiv login again and paste the new code right after logging in.

pixivLoginExpired.what: The login wasn’t started or is too old.
pixivLoginExpired.cause: The code only fits the Pixiv login opened last, and that lasts 15 minutes.
pixivLoginExpired.action: Click “Open Pixiv login” and start again.

pixivLoginFailed.cause: Pixiv couldn’t be reached or answered something unexpected.
pixivLoginFailed.action: Try again in a few minutes. If it keeps failing, updating the tools often helps.

pixivTokenInvalid.what: That doesn’t look like a Pixiv token.
pixivTokenInvalid.cause: A refresh token only has letters, digits, “-” and “_” and is at least 20 characters long.
pixivTokenInvalid.action: Copy the token again completely – without quotes or spaces.

pdfBroken.cause: The file is damaged, not fully downloaded, or not a real PDF.
pdfBroken.action: Open it in a PDF program and save it again (or use “Print to PDF”), then try once more.

pdfNoPages.cause: There is no page left for the new PDF.

pdfImageBroken.what: The picture couldn’t be added as a page.
pdfImageBroken.cause: The image file is damaged or a special case the PDF tool doesn’t know (e.g. a CMYK JPG or a PNG with an unusual colour depth).
pdfImageBroken.action: Convert the picture to a normal JPG or PNG under “Convert”, then add it.

pdfWrongType.what: This file is neither a PDF nor a JPG or PNG picture.
pdfWrongType.cause: Only PDFs and photos can be made into pages here.
pdfWrongType.action: Convert the file to PDF, JPG or PNG under “Convert” first.

ocrFailed.cause: The PDF is built in an unusual way, very large, or the server ran out of memory.
ocrFailed.action: Try fewer pages at once, or set “Pages that already have text” (expert mode) to “Recognise everything as pictures again”.

ocrHasText.cause: The pages already have a text layer, so nothing was recognised.
ocrHasText.action: If the existing recognition is poor, choose “Recognise the text again” in expert mode.

ocrMissing.what: Text recognition isn’t fully set up on the server.
ocrMissing.cause: A required program (Tesseract or a language pack) is missing.
ocrMissing.action: Ask the admin to rebuild the Conbert image (docker compose up --build).

whisperFailed.cause: The sound couldn’t be processed, or the server ran out of memory (large models need a lot of RAM).
whisperFailed.action: Try again, or ask the admin to pick a smaller speech model in the settings.

noSpeech.what: No speech was found in the recording.
noSpeech.cause: There is only music, noise or silence – or the speech is very quiet.
noSpeech.action: Check that the right part is selected and set the spoken language yourself.

whisperDownloadRunning.what: The model is being downloaded right now.
whisperDownloadRunning.cause: It can’t be deleted while it downloads.
whisperDownloadRunning.action: Wait until the download has finished.

modelDownload.what: The AI model couldn’t be downloaded.
modelDownload.cause: The server can’t reach the internet, the source (Hugging Face or GitHub) is unreachable, or the file arrived damaged (the checksum didn’t match).
modelDownload.action: Try again later. Without internet, the admin can put the model into the folder /data/models by hand.

modelUnknown.what: Conbert doesn’t know this AI model.
modelUnknown.cause: The setting points to a model that doesn’t exist (any more).
modelUnknown.action: Pick another model in the settings.

imageAiFailed.cause: The picture couldn’t be processed, or the server ran out of memory.
imageAiFailed.action: Try again with a smaller picture or without upscaling.

imageTooLargeToUpscale.what: The picture is too big to upscale.
imageTooLargeToUpscale.cause: The result would have more than 64 megapixels (8000 × 8000) – too much memory and time.
imageTooLargeToUpscale.action: Use 2× instead of 4×, or make the picture smaller first.

invalidToken.what: The API token is not valid.
invalidToken.cause: It was copied wrong, has expired or was deleted.
invalidToken.action: Create a new token under Settings → API access.

tokenNotAllowed.what: That doesn’t work with an API token.
tokenNotAllowed.cause: Tokens may not manage tokens, users, passwords or keys – so a lost token doesn’t open the whole account.
tokenNotAllowed.action: Sign in normally in the browser for this.

quotaExceeded.what: Your storage on the server is full.
quotaExceeded.cause: You already have as many files and results on the server as your quota allows.
quotaExceeded.action: Download finished results and remove them from the list, or wait until Conbert cleans up (after about an hour). The admin can give you more space.

serverOutOfMemory.what: The server ran out of memory with this file.
serverOutOfMemory.cause: The file is very large, or several big conversions are running at once. The container's memory limit (CONBERT_MEMORY_LIMIT) may also be set too low.
serverOutOfMemory.action: Try again when less is going on, or choose a smaller resolution. If it happens often: give the server more memory or set CONBERT_JOB_CONCURRENCY to 1.

blenderMissing.what: Blender isn't installed on the server.
blenderMissing.cause: Blender is only downloaded on request because it is very large.
blenderMissing.action: Ask an admin to install Blender under Administration → Blender.

blenderUnsupported.what: Blender can't be installed on this server.
blenderUnsupported.cause: Official Linux versions exist only for x64 processors, not for ARM (e.g. Raspberry Pi or many NAS).
blenderUnsupported.action: For .blend, USD and Alembic files, run Conbert on an x64 machine. The other 3D formats work without Blender.

blenderRunning.what: Blender is being installed right now.
blenderRunning.cause: It can't be removed during the installation.
blenderRunning.action: Wait until the installation is finished.

blenderNoSpace.what: There isn't enough free space for Blender.
blenderNoSpace.cause: The download and the unpacked program need about 1.7 GB in the data folder together.
blenderNoSpace.action: Free up space in the data folder (e.g. delete old results or AI models) and try again.

blenderDownload.cause: The server can't reach the internet, download.blender.org isn't reachable, or the file arrived damaged (the checksum didn't match).

blenderInstall.cause: Something went wrong while unpacking – usually the disk is full or the data folder isn't writable.
blenderInstall.action: Check the free space in the data folder and try again. The server log has the details.

modelEmpty.what: There is no 3D model in the file.
modelEmpty.cause: The file only contains a camera, lights or empty objects – or the objects are in a form Blender doesn't treat as a model.
modelEmpty.action: Open the file in a 3D program and check whether it has visible objects.

viewFailed.cause: Usually Conbert was just updated while the page was open, or the connection to the server dropped for a moment.
viewFailed.action: Reload the page. If that doesn’t help, send the details below to whoever looks after your Conbert server.

subtitlesEmpty.what: No subtitles were found in the file.
subtitlesEmpty.cause: The file is empty, has a different format than its ending says, or the shift moved all subtitles before the start.
subtitlesEmpty.action: Open the file in a text editor and check that it contains times like “00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:02,000”. When shifting, use a smaller value.

subtitlesNoTrack.what: This video has no built-in subtitles (or not that many).
subtitlesNoTrack.cause: Not every video comes with subtitles; MP4s from phones or YouTube usually have none.
subtitlesNoTrack.action: Set “Where do the subtitles come from?” to “Automatic” or “Recognise speech” – then speech recognition writes them from the spoken words.

subtitlesImageTrack.what: These subtitles are pictures, not text.
subtitlesImageTrack.cause: DVDs and Blu-rays often store subtitles as small pictures. Conbert can’t turn those into SRT, VTT or ASS.
subtitlesImageTrack.action: Pick another subtitle track if there is one, or have the subtitles written anew with “Recognise speech”.

subtitlesExtractFailed.what: The subtitles couldn’t be taken out of the video.
subtitlesExtractFailed.cause: The subtitle track is damaged or in a format ffmpeg doesn’t know.
subtitlesExtractFailed.action: Try “Recognise speech”. “Show details” tells you what ffmpeg reported.

attachmentInvalid.what: The extra file you chose doesn’t fit here.
attachmentInvalid.cause: It has a different format than allowed, e.g. a video instead of a subtitle file.
attachmentInvalid.action: Choose a file with one of the endings shown (e.g. .srt) and try again.

attachmentGone.what: The extra file you chose is no longer on the server.
