attachmentGone.cause: The server tidies up uploaded files after a while.
attachmentGone.action: Start the conversion again – the file is then uploaded anew.

downloadDeviantartLogin.cause: Either no login is set up yet, or it ran out. A DeviantArt login lasts about three months.
downloadDeviantartLogin.action: Log in again in the settings under “Download” → “DeviantArt access”.

deviantartAppInvalid.what: That doesn't look like a DeviantArt access.
deviantartAppInvalid.cause: “client_id” is a number, “client_secret” has 32 characters (digits and letters a–f).
deviantartAppInvalid.action: Copy both values from DeviantArt's developer page again – without spaces.

deviantartAppRefused.cause: “client_id” or “client_secret” is wrong, or the app was deleted at DeviantArt.
deviantartAppRefused.action: Open DeviantArt's developer page, check your app and copy both values again. If everything is right, DeviantArt may be having trouble – then try again later.

deviantartAppMissing.what: No DeviantArt access of your own is set up yet.
deviantartAppMissing.cause: A login always belongs to your own access (app).
deviantartAppMissing.action: First set up your app with “Set up your own access”.

deviantartCodeInvalid.what: That is no address from the DeviantArt login.
deviantartCodeInvalid.cause: The field doesn't contain the address with “code=”, or only part of it.
deviantartCodeInvalid.action: Copy the whole address from the login tab's address bar and paste it again.

deviantartCodeExpired.what: The login code has run out.
deviantartCodeExpired.cause: A code only lasts a short time and works only once.
deviantartCodeExpired.action: Open the DeviantArt login again and paste the new address right after.

deviantartLoginExpired.cause: The address belongs to an older login, or the login is older than 15 minutes.
deviantartLoginExpired.action: Click “Open DeviantArt login” and start again.

deviantartLoginFailed.cause: DeviantArt couldn't be reached or answered something unexpected.
deviantartLoginFailed.action: Try again in a few minutes.

featureForbidden.what: This function is blocked for you.
featureForbidden.cause: Your administrator switched it off for your account or your group.
featureForbidden.action: Ask your administrator to unlock it for you.

groupNameTaken.what: There already is a group with this name.
groupNameTaken.cause: Group names must be unique (upper and lower case don't count).

groupBuiltin.what: The group “All users” can't be changed like that.
groupBuiltin.cause: Everyone is a member automatically. It can't be renamed or deleted and has no members of its own.
groupBuiltin.action: Only switch functions on or off here. For everything else, create an own group.

ldapManaged.what: This account's password isn't managed in Conbert.
ldapManaged.cause: The person signs in through LDAP or your reverse proxy.
ldapManaged.action: Change the password where the account really lives (e.g. in Active Directory).

ldapUnreachable.what: The LDAP server can't be reached.
ldapUnreachable.cause: The address is wrong, the server is off, or a firewall blocks the port.
ldapUnreachable.action: Check the address in the administration under “Sign-in through LDAP” and test the connection. Local Conbert accounts keep working.

ldapTls.what: The encrypted connection to the LDAP server failed.
ldapTls.cause: Usually the server's certificate is self-signed or doesn't match the address.
ldapTls.action: Enter your server's CA certificate or switch off “Check the server's certificate” (less secure).

ldapBindFailed.what: Conbert couldn't sign in to the LDAP server with the service account.
ldapBindFailed.cause: The bind DN or the service account's password is wrong.
ldapBindFailed.action: Check the service account and password. With Active Directory the form name@company.com often works, too.

ldapSearchFailed.cause: The search base or filter is invalid, or the service account may not search there.
ldapSearchFailed.action: Check the search base and filters (e.g. with a template) and test the connection.

ldapNotConfigured.what: Sign-in through LDAP isn't set up yet.
ldapNotConfigured.cause: The address, search base or user filter is missing, or LDAP is switched off.
ldapNotConfigured.action: Set up LDAP in the administration and switch it on.

archiveZipTooBig.what: That is too much for one ZIP file.
archiveZipTooBig.cause: All files together are bigger than 4 GB – Conbert cannot pack ZIP files that big.
archiveZipTooBig.action: Download the files one by one, or first delete what you already have.

contactKeyInvalid.what: That isn't a valid public key.
contactKeyInvalid.cause: Public age keys start with “age1”. Maybe a piece got lost while copying – or it's a private key (AGE-SECRET-KEY-…), which never belongs in the contact book.
contactKeyInvalid.action: Ask for the public key again and paste all of it.

contactExists.what: This key is already in your contact book.
contactExists.cause: Every key appears only once. “Show details” tells you under which name.
contactExists.action: Rename the existing contact if the name no longer fits.

contactLimit.action: Delete contacts you no longer need.

stages.downloadingModel: Downloading the speech model (first time only) …

auth.usernameHint: 2–32 characters: letters without accents, digits, dot, underscore, hyphen.
auth.displayNameHint: How your name is shown in Conbert, e.g. “Anna”.
auth.passwordHint: At least {{min}} characters. Tip: a short sentence is secure and easy to remember.
auth.passwordTooShort: Still too short – at least {{min}} characters.

setup.title: Welcome to Conbert!
setup.intro: Before you start, create the administrator account once. With it you can later create accounts for other people.
setup.codeHint: It's in the server log, e.g. “K7QM-3XRP”.
setup.codeHelp: The code makes sure only you – and not just anyone on the network – can set up Conbert. You'll find it in the server output: with Docker, run “docker compose logs conbert” in Conbert's folder.
setup.modeLocalHelp: Everyone gets a user name and password in Conbert.
setup.modeProxyHelp: Your proxy signs people in. You become administrator as “{{user}}”; others get an account automatically on their first visit.
setup.proxyNotDetected: Reverse-proxy sign-in is configured, but this request didn't come through the proxy. Open Conbert via your proxy's address to choose this option.

login.title: Sign in
login.intro: Sign in with your Conbert account.
login.proxyIntro: Sign-in is handled by your reverse proxy.
login.forgot: Forgot your password? An administrator can set a new one under Administration.
login.introLdap: Sign in with your Conbert account or your directory account (LDAP).

account.title: Your account
account.otherDevices: You'll be signed out on your other devices afterwards.
account.proxyUser: You sign in through the reverse proxy. Manage your password there.
account.ldapUser: You sign in with your directory account (LDAP). You change your password there.

users.title: Manage users
users.intro: Everyone has their own settings and only sees their own files and jobs. With “Groups & permissions” you decide which groups someone is in and what they may use.
users.addIntro: Give the person their user name and a starting password. They can change it themselves afterwards.
users.initialPasswordHint: At least {{min}} characters. Share it with the person in a safe way.
users.roleHelp: Administrators can add and delete users and reset passwords. Users can use Conbert normally.
users.resetPasswordIntro: The person is signed out everywhere and must sign in with the new password.
users.passwordReset: The password of “{{name}}” has been reset.
users.deleteWarning: The account is deleted together with all settings, uploaded files and jobs. This can't be undone.
users.resetBooruPinIntro: The PIN this person used to lock their booru age ratings is removed. The chosen ratings stay as they are; the person can set a new PIN afterwards.
users.booruPinReset: The booru PIN of “{{name}}” was removed.
users.addGroupsHint: Optional. You can change the groups any time later with “Groups & permissions”.
users.accessIntro: Choose the person's groups. For single functions you can also decide that they are allowed or blocked no matter what the groups say.
users.adminAll: Administrators may always do everything. The settings here only apply once the person is a normal user again.
users.noGroups: No own groups yet. You create them in the administration under “Groups”.
users.functionsHelp: “Like the groups” = allowed as long as none of the person's groups blocks it. “Always allow” and “Always block” win over the groups. The dot on the left shows what applies in the end.

archive.moved_one: Downloaded – the file stays in the archive.
archive.moved_other: Downloaded – {{count}} files stay in the archive.
archive.intro: Everything you converted or compressed, ready to download again. It stays saved in this browser (even after reloading) until you remove it, but at most {{days}} days. None of it is stored on the server.
archive.empty: Nothing in the archive yet. As soon as a conversion or compression is finished, the result lands here.
archive.clearText_one: The file will be deleted from this browser. This can't be undone.
archive.clearText_other: All {{count}} files will be deleted from this browser. This can't be undone.

server.intro: Downloads you loaded without a storage location. They are on your server, count against your storage quota and are deleted automatically after the keeping time – download what you want to keep.
server.empty: Nothing on the server yet. Choose “Server archive” when downloading; the files land here and stay {{time}}.
server.clearText_one: The file is deleted from the server. This cannot be undone.
server.clearText_other: All {{count}} files are deleted from the server. This cannot be undone.

history.intro: Every job from the last {{days}} days with its settings – including the ones that didn't work. Use “Again” to convert a file with exactly the same settings. Only the settings are kept, no files, and only in this browser.
history.empty: No jobs in the history yet. As soon as you convert or compress something, it shows up here – with all its settings.
history.clearText: All history entries are deleted from this browser. The files in the archive stay.
history.ready_one: The file is ready with the old settings. Check it quickly, then click “Convert”.
history.ready_other: {{count}} files are ready with the old settings. Check them quickly, then click “Convert”.

trim.title: Trim
trim.intro: Choose the part you want to keep: drag the two handles, type a time, or play the file and click “Start here” or “End here” at the right moment. Then pick the target format as usual – the same format works too, or GIF/WebP for a short animation.
trim.timeHint: Time as minutes:seconds, e.g. 1:05 – or just seconds like 65.
trim.invalidTime: That's not a valid time. Examples: 1:05, 0:30.5 or 65.
trim.notPlayable: Your browser can't play this file. You can still type the start and end as times – the cut happens when converting.

fast.label: Cut fast (no re-encoding)
fast.help: The file is only cut, not recalculated. That takes seconds and the quality stays exactly the same. The catch: a video can only start at a key frame (a picture that doesn't need the ones before it). So the part sometimes starts a few seconds earlier.
fast.effect: On: lightning fast with the same quality, but the start is not exact. Off: exact to a tenth of a second, but slower because the video is recalculated.
fast.onlySame: Only works when the format stays the same (e.g. MP4 → MP4).

still.help: Saves the picture currently shown in the player as a PNG in full resolution. Move to the right moment first and pause the video.
still.failed: The still picture couldn't be saved. Try again at another moment.

pdf.intro: Merge PDFs, split them or tidy them up: sort, turn and delete pages. Photos (JPG/PNG) become pages too. Everything happens on your device – the files are not sent to the server.
pdf.dragHint: To sort, drag a page to another place – or use the arrows below the page.
pdf.pagesLabel: Pages in the order of the new PDF

merge.label: All pages as one PDF
merge.help: To merge: all pages in the order above, with your turns.

selected.label_one: Only the selected page as a PDF
selected.label_other: Only the {{count}} selected pages as one PDF
selected.help: Tick the pages you need above. The others are left out.

each.label: Every page as its own PDF
each.help: Splits everything into single pages. You get them together as a ZIP file.

ranges.label: Split by ranges
ranges.help: You decide which pages go into one file together – e.g. chapter 1 and chapter 2 separately.
ranges.fieldHelp: Type the page numbers as shown at the top of the cards. A comma separates the files: “1-3, 4-6” makes two PDFs. “8-” means “from page 8 to the end”, “5” is page 5 alone.
ranges.invalid: That doesn’t fit. Write ranges like “1-3, 5, 8-” – with pages between 1 and {{count}}.

ocr.label: Make text recognisable (OCR)
ocr.help: For scans and photos of documents: Conbert reads the text in the pictures and lays it invisibly over the page. Afterwards you can search the PDF (Ctrl+F) and select and copy text. The pages look the same as before.
ocr.hint: Runs on your server – the finished PDF is sent there for this. Depending on the number of pages it takes a few seconds to a few minutes.
ocr.unavailable: Not available: this needs your Conbert server with text recognition. Check that the server can be reached.

preview.intro: This is what the file looks like. None of it leaves your device.
preview.compareSlider: Move the line between before and after
preview.documentHint: The first document preview loads the document tool once (about 58 MB).
preview.truncated: The file is very long – the preview only shows the beginning.
preview.notAvailable: There is no preview for “{{format}}” yet. You can still convert and download the file.
preview.model3d: 3D model – rotate with the mouse or a finger, zoom with the wheel or two fingers
preview.modelHint: Drag = rotate, right-click/two fingers = move, wheel/pinch = zoom in. Textures from separate files are missing in the preview.
preview.fontSample: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

nav.label: What do you want to do?

compress.intro: Make files smaller – usually in the same format, e.g. so they fit into an email or take up less space.
compress.listHint: Choose for each file how much to shrink it. If a file would get bigger, Conbert keeps the original.
compress.formatHelp: Usually the format stays the same (a PNG becomes a smaller PNG). Modern formats like WebP, AVIF or Opus often save much more space – but don't open in every older program.
compress.notPossible: Conbert can't compress “{{format}}” yet. The “Convert” tab may offer a smaller format.
compress.expertHint: Fine-tuning – these settings win over the chosen level:
compress.keptOriginal: It couldn't get any smaller – the original was already packed well. Conbert kept it unchanged.
compress.targetMissed: It couldn’t get any smaller without making the file useless. Try a slightly bigger target size or a more modern format (e.g. WebP, AVIF or Opus).

level.label: How much smaller?
level.help: The smaller the file should be, the more detail is lost. For photos and videos “Balanced” is usually hard to notice.
level.maxHelp: Shrinks carefully – you'll practically see and hear no difference.
level.balancedHelp: Much smaller with hardly visible differences. The best choice in most cases.
level.smallHelp: As small as possible. Pictures and sound get visibly or audibly worse, large videos are reduced to 720p.
level.targetHelp: You say how big the file may be at most, e.g. 10 MB for an e-mail attachment. Conbert looks for the best quality that still fits – for pictures it also lowers the resolution if needed.

compress.targetSizeHelp: The finished file may be at most this big. Example: 10 MB for an e-mail attachment or 500 KB for an upload form. 1 MB is 1024 KB. Conbert never makes the file bigger than this and stays as close to it as it can.
compress.targetLevels: Conbert can’t set an exact size for this format. It tries the levels from “Maximum quality” to “Smallest” and takes the best one that fits. If none fits, you get the smallest.
compress.alreadySmall: The file is already smaller than the target size. Conbert leaves it as it is.
compress.targetMissedLevels: This format couldn’t get any smaller – this is the smallest level. Conbert can’t set an exact size here.

smb.name: Network folder (SMB)
smb.summary: A shared folder in your home network – e.g. on your NAS (Synology, QNAP), router or a Windows PC.

sftp.name: SFTP server
sftp.summary: Secure file access over SSH – e.g. on a Linux server, Raspberry Pi or NAS.

ftp.name: FTP / FTPS
ftp.summary: An older way to transfer files – e.g. on older NAS devices or rented web space.

webdav.name: Nextcloud / WebDAV
webdav.summary: Your own cloud like Nextcloud or ownCloud, or another WebDAV storage.

s3.name: S3 storage
s3.summary: Object storage like MinIO, Amazon S3, Backblaze B2 or Wasabi – good for backups.

local.name: Folder on the server
local.summary: A folder mounted into the Conbert container – e.g. a hard drive or an NFS mount.

smb.address: The address of the shared folder, as you'd type it in Windows Explorer or Finder. Conbert needs the folder name after the device (the “share”).
smb.user: The user you sign in to the NAS or PC with. Leave empty if the share is open to guests.
smb.password: That user's password. Conbert stores it encrypted and never shows it again.
smb.domain: Only needed in company networks. At home, “WORKGROUP” (the default) almost always fits.
smb.port: Usually 445. Only change it if your NAS uses another port.

sftp.host: Name or IP address of the server, e.g. “nas.local” or “192.168.1.20”.
sftp.user: Your user name on the server (as when signing in via SSH).
sftp.password: The password – or leave it empty and give an SSH key instead. Stored encrypted.
sftp.privateKey: Instead of a password: the content of your private key file (e.g. id_ed25519), without a passphrase. Stored encrypted.

ftp.host: Name or IP address of the FTP server, e.g. “ftp.example.com”.
ftp.security: Whether the connection is encrypted. Without encryption, someone on the network can read the password and files – only use it in your own home network.
ftp.skipCertificateCheck: Only turn this on if your device uses a self-made certificate and the connection fails otherwise. Conbert then no longer checks that it really talks to your device.
ftp.port: Leave empty for the default (21, or 990 for implicit FTPS).

webdav.url: The WebDAV address. In Nextcloud you'll find it at the bottom left under “Files settings → WebDAV”.
webdav.vendor: Which software runs there, so dates and checksums work properly.
webdav.password: Ideally an app password (Nextcloud: Settings → Security → “Create new app password”). Stored encrypted.

s3.provider: Which service the storage is at.
s3.endpoint: The address of the S3 server. Leave empty for Amazon S3.
s3.bucket: The name of the bucket (the storage “container”). Conbert doesn't create it – it must exist already.
s3.accessKeyId: The public part of your access key.
s3.secretAccessKey: The secret part of your access key. Stored encrypted.
s3.region: Only needed if your provider asks for a region (e.g. “eu-central-1”).

local.root: A folder your administrator mounted into the Conbert container (in docker-compose.yml under “volumes”). Only these folders are allowed.

browser.truncated: This folder has a great many files – Conbert only shows the first 2,000.
browser.selectAll_one: Select the file in this folder
browser.selectAll_other: Select all {{count}} files in this folder

card.title: Storage locations
card.intro: Save results straight to your NAS, your server or your cloud – and open files from there. Passwords are stored encrypted.
card.empty: No storage locations yet. Add one, e.g. a folder on your NAS.
card.deleteText: Conbert only forgets the connection and the stored password. The files on the storage location stay where they are.

wizard.title: Add a storage location

steps.type: Step 1 of 3: Where should your files go?
steps.connection: Step 2 of 3: How does Conbert get there? “Test connection” tells you right away if everything is right.
steps.folder: Step 3 of 3: Pick the folder and give the storage location a name.

wizard.moreInExpertMode: More settings (port, domain, SSH key …) are in expert mode.
wizard.startFolderHelp: Only needed if the folder isn't inside your user folder – e.g. “/volume1” on Synology. Leave empty for the user folder.
wizard.folderHelp: Click your way to the folder Conbert should save to and open files from. Conbert never leaves this folder.
wizard.name: Name
wizard.asTargetHelp: Shows up as “Save to …” next to the download button.
wizard.asSourceHelp: Shows up as “Open from storage” next to the drop area.
wizard.defaultHelp: Preselected when saving. Later, downloads (e.g. from social media) will also land here automatically.
wizard.conflictHelp: What should happen if the folder already has a file with the same name.
wizard.patternHelp: Conbert puts the files into subfolders automatically. Placeholders: {date} (2026-10-27), {year}, {month}, {day}, {category} (image, video …), {ext} (png …), {platform} (youtube …), {source} (channel, profile or thread). Example: {year}/{category}. Leave empty = straight into the folder. Downloads also go into a folder named after the channel, profile or thread – unless {source} is in the pattern already.
wizard.noRoots: No folder is mounted into the Conbert container yet. Mount a folder under /storage in docker-compose.yml (guide in docs/) and restart Conbert.

save.title: Save to storage location
save.privacyHint: To save to your storage location, the finished file is sent through your server.

open.title: Open from storage location
open.intro: Pick one or more files. They are loaded through your server and then show up in the list like uploaded files.
open.previewHint: Click a file to look at it here.

autoSave.label: Save every conversion automatically
autoSave.help: Every finished result is also put on this storage location – even when it was converted on your device. The file is sent there through your server. You can still download it.
autoSave.skipped: The file already existed on “{{name}}” – skipped.

quick.oneUse: At least one must stay on – otherwise Conbert can't do anything with the location. If you don't need it any more, remove it.
quick.nowDefault: “{{name}}” is now your default storage location.

metadata.loading: Reading metadata … (the first time, the tool is loaded, about 25 MB)
metadata.gpsWarning: This file tells where it was taken (GPS location). If you share it, anyone who looks can see that.
metadata.notWritable: Conbert can't write metadata into {{format}} (yet) – you can only look at it here.

title.label: Title
title.help: The name of the work, e.g. “Sunset at the sea”. Many photo and music apps show it instead of the file name.

description.label: Description
description.help: A few sentences about the content. Helps when searching and for people who can't see the picture.

author.label: Creator
author.help: Who made the photo, video or document.

copyright.label: Copyright
copyright.help: Who owns the rights, e.g. “© 2026 Anna Example”.

keywords.label: Keywords
keywords.help: Words to find it again, separated by commas – e.g. “holiday, sea, family”. Photo managers like digiKam or Lightroom can search for them.

date.label: Date taken
date.help: When the photo or video was taken. Gallery apps sort by it.

metadata.removeGpsHelp: Deletes the GPS data so nobody can see where it was taken. Good before sharing photos.
metadata.removeAllHelp: Deletes everything the file tells about itself (camera, date, place, programs …). The fields above are still written if you fill them in.
metadata.written: Metadata was written into the file.

tagNames.Title: Title
tagNames.Creator: Creator
tagNames.Subject: Subject / keywords
tagNames.Author: Author
tagNames.MIMEType: MIME type (file kind for the web)

metadata.fieldNotWritable: This format has no such field (e.g. music files have no keywords).

downloader.title: Download
downloader.intro: Paste a link from YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, X, Pixiv, 4chan and more. Conbert shows you first what it finds – the files then land in your list and can be converted right away.
downloader.legalHint: Only download content you have the rights to or may use privately.
downloader.checking: Conbert is looking at what's behind the link …

quality.label: Quality
quality.help: How good picture and sound will be. Higher = nicer, but bigger files. For phones, 720p is usually plenty.
quality.bestHelp: The best the site offers (up to 4K). As MP4 when possible.
quality.1080Help: Sharp on big screens, medium file size.
quality.720Help: Good for phones and tablets, much smaller files.
quality.audioHelp: Loads only the sound and saves it as MP3 – e.g. for music or podcasts.

parts.label: What to load?
parts.help: Which parts of the profile to load. Stories and highlights almost always need a login (cookies).

limit.label: At most
limit.help: Conbert loads at most this many items – so nobody loads thousands of files by accident.
limit.many: That's a lot of files. Large amounts take long and can make your account look suspicious to the site.

period.label: Period (optional)
period.help: Only load posts from this period.

downloader.needsCookies: This link usually needs a login. Add your cookies for {{platform}} in the settings.
downloader.hasCookies: Your stored cookies for {{platform}} are used.
downloader.skipped_one: {{count}} file was too big and was skipped.
downloader.skipped_other: {{count}} files were too big and were skipped.
downloader.added_one: {{count}} file is now in your list.
downloader.added_other: {{count}} files are now in your list.
downloader.gone: The files are no longer on the server (they are deleted after a while).

settings.title: Download
settings.intro: Logins for private content (cookies and your Pixiv account), pauses between requests and the tools yt-dlp and gallery-dl.
settings.sleepHelp: Conbert waits this many seconds between two requests to a site. Longer pauses protect your account from being blocked.
settings.cookiesHelp: For private or login-only content (e.g. Instagram stories) Conbert needs your login. You never enter your password – you only export the cookies from your browser. They are stored encrypted and never shown again.
settings.toolsHelp: Websites change often. When downloads suddenly fail, an update usually helps.
settings.updated: The tools are up to date.

guide.title: How to get your cookies.txt
guide.intro: Cookies are small notes a site uses to recognise that you're signed in. With them, Conbert can load content only signed-in users see.
guide.step1: Install the browser extension “Get cookies.txt LOCALLY” – for Chrome, Edge and Brave from the Chrome Web Store, for Firefox from addons.mozilla.org. It works only on your device and sends nothing anywhere.
guide.step2: Open the site (e.g. instagram.com) and sign in as usual.
guide.step3: Click the extension's icon at the top right, then “Export”. A file like “instagram.com_cookies.txt” is saved.
guide.step4: Upload that file here for the matching platform with “Upload cookies.txt”.
guide.step5: Delete the file from your computer afterwards.
guide.warning: Important: these cookies let anyone sign in as you. Never share the file. If you sign out on the site, they stop working – then just export them again.
guide.platforms: Each site needs its own file: export Instagram cookies on instagram.com, Reddit cookies on reddit.com and so on. Instagram and Reddit threads can hardly be loaded without cookies anymore – YouTube, TikTok & co. usually work without.

destination.label: Save to
destination.help: Where the files go. Each file is passed on as soon as it is done – not only at the end. Downloading always happens on your server, never in your browser. “Server archive” is a temporary store on your server: handy when you only need the files on this device and have no storage location (NAS …) set up. After the keeping time, Conbert deletes them by itself.
destination.list: Conversion list (the files are loaded into this browser)
destination.listMany: With many files your browser loads them all. For whole channels a storage location is usually the better choice.
destination.onlyTargets: The files only go to the storage location and are deleted from the server afterwards.
destination.server: Server archive (no storage location – stays {{time}}, then deleted automatically)
destination.serverHint: The files stay on your server, even when you close this page. You find them under Archive → On the server and can download them there.

downloader.skipKnownHelp: Conbert remembers what you downloaded from this platform and doesn't load it again. If the same file (same name, same size) is already at the storage location, it isn't saved twice either. Switch it off if you deliberately want to load everything again (e.g. in another quality).
downloader.nothingNew: Nothing new – everything had been downloaded before.

ugoira.label: Save animated pictures as
ugoira.help: Pixiv has its own animated pictures (“Ugoira”): a series of frames with timing. Conbert turns them into a normal file that plays everywhere.
ugoira.mp4Help: Plays on every phone and computer, small and in good quality.
ugoira.gifHelp: Works everywhere, even in chats and forums – but often gets big and has only 256 colours.
ugoira.webmHelp: Very good quality and small, plays in browsers but not on every iPhone.
ugoira.zipHelp: The original frames without conversion, e.g. for further editing.

adult.label: Also load works for adults (18+)
adult.help: Pixiv marks works for adults (R-18 and R-18G). Without the tick, Conbert skips them. With it, they only come if they are switched on in your Pixiv account as well.

settings.title: Pixiv account
settings.help: Pixiv lets you load almost nothing unless you are logged in. Instead of cookies, Pixiv needs a login key of its own. You log in on Pixiv’s own page for it – Conbert never sees your password. The key is stored encrypted and never shown again.
settings.codeLabel: Paste the code or address here
settings.tokenLabel: I already have a refresh token
settings.tokenHelp: For advanced users: a Pixiv refresh token you made yourself, e.g. with “gallery-dl oauth:pixiv”, can be pasted here directly.

guide.intro: This is how you connect your Pixiv account. It takes about two minutes and works best on a computer with Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
guide.step1: Click “Open Pixiv login” below. A new tab opens with Pixiv’s login page.
guide.step2: In that new tab, press F12 (on a Mac: ⌥ + ⌘ + I). The developer tools open at the side. Switch to the “Console” tab there.
guide.step3: Now log in to Pixiv as usual. Afterwards nothing seems to happen – that is how it should be. A red message with “pixiv://account/login?code=…” appears in the console.
guide.step4: Copy the whole address starting at “pixiv://” (or just the part after “code=”), come back to this tab and paste it into the field below. Conbert connects right away.
guide.step5: Nothing in the console (e.g. in Firefox)? Switch to the “Network” tab and click the last entry “callback?state=…”. The code is there as well.
guide.hurry: Be quick: the code only lasts 30 seconds after logging in. If it didn’t work, simply open the login again.

downloader.sharedLink: Took the link from the share menu – checking …
downloader.deviantartHint: DeviantArt: Without your own access, Conbert uses gallery-dl's, which every gallery-dl user in the world shares. When it is busy, the download pauses again and again and can take hours. It keeps going, though, even after a restart. Mature or private works are skipped. Your own access (set up once, about 5 minutes) helps with both.
downloader.deviantartOwnHint: Your own DeviantArt access is used. Works marked as mature or private only come once you also log in to DeviantArt.

settings.title: DeviantArt access
settings.help: gallery-dl loads pictures through DeviantArt's official interface. Without your own access you share gallery-dl's with every other user – it is often busy, and mature works are missing. With a small “app” of your own at DeviantArt, the access is yours alone. If you also log in, mature and private works come too. You only type your password on DeviantArt's page; Conbert stores everything encrypted and never shows the secret again.
settings.shared: gallery-dl's shared access (often busy, no mature works)
settings.ownApp: your own access (app {{id}}), not logged in
settings.connectedAs: your own access, logged in as {{name}} (since {{date}})
settings.logout: Log out of DeviantArt (the access stays)
settings.codeLabel: Paste the address from the address bar here
settings.loggedOut: You are logged out of DeviantArt. Your own access stays.

appGuide.intro: This is how you set up your own DeviantArt access. You need a DeviantArt account, and it takes about 5 minutes – best on a computer.
appGuide.step1: Log in to DeviantArt and open the developer page (“Applications & Keys”).
appGuide.step3: Under “OAuth2 Redirect URI Whitelist”, enter exactly this address. It belongs to gallery-dl and only passes you on after logging in:
appGuide.step4: Enter a name under “Title”, e.g. “Conbert”. If the page asks for other required fields (e.g. a description), write something short. Agree to the terms at the very bottom and click “Save”.
appGuide.step5: DeviantArt now shows “client_id” (a number) and “client_secret” (32 digits and letters). Copy both into the fields below and click “Check and save”.

loginGuide.intro: With the login, Conbert also loads works marked as mature or only visible to logged-in users.
loginGuide.step1: Click “Open DeviantArt login” below. A new tab opens.
loginGuide.step2: Log in to DeviantArt (if needed) and allow access with “Authorize”.
loginGuide.step3: Then the tab ends up on a page that doesn't load (“localhost”, “this site can't be reached”). That's how it should be.
loginGuide.step4: Copy the whole address from that tab's address bar (it contains “code=”), come back here and paste it below. Conbert connects right away.

downloader.recordOnly_one: First run of the subscription: 1 existing work remembered. Existing works are not downloaded here – the subscription only loads what is added from now on.
downloader.recordOnly_other: First run of the subscription: {{count}} existing works remembered. Existing works are not downloaded here – the subscription only loads what is added from now on.

ratings.generalHelp: Suitable for everyone. On Konachan and yande.re this is called “safe”.
ratings.sensitiveHelp: A bit more revealing, e.g. swimwear – but nothing sexual.
ratings.questionableHelp: Clearly suggestive, sometimes with nudity. Adults only.

speed.normalHelp: As fast as the site allows. Good for small searches.
speed.slowHelp: One request every 2 seconds. For big searches without a premium account – takes longer, but gets everything.
speed.very-slowHelp: One request every 10 seconds. For huge collections that run in the background overnight.

sidecar.jsonHelp: All details of the picture (tags, artist, source, rating) as a .json file next to it – good as a backup.
sidecar.txtHelp: The tags, comma-separated, in a .txt file next to it – e.g. for picture catalogues or AI datasets.
sidecar.embedHelp: Writes the tags as keywords right into the picture file. Photo managers like digiKam or Lightroom can then find them.
sidecar.label: Also save tags
sidecar.help: Source, artist and the post link are always written into the file (where the format allows it). Here you choose whether the tags are saved too.
sidecar.onlyTargets: JSON and text files only go to storage locations, not into the list.

siteHelp.gelbooru: Very large collection. Needs a free API key.

booru.title: Booru
booru.intro: Download pictures from Safebooru, Gelbooru, Konachan & co. – one by link or as a search by tags. You see a preview first and choose what is loaded.
booru.onlyGeneralHint: You only see all-ages content. You can change that in the settings.
booru.tagLimit_one: Up to {{count}} tag per search goes to the site – Conbert checks the rest itself.
booru.tagLimit_other: Up to {{count}} tags per search go to the site – Conbert checks the rest itself.
booru.needsAccountLink: Enter an API key in the settings

search.placeholder: Tags, e.g. cat_ears blue_eyes – or a link to a post

form.toggleHelp: Instead of typing search commands, pick tags and filters here. The text field above is filled in automatically – both stay the same.
form.includeHelp: Tags every picture must have, e.g. “cat_ears”. Several tags = all must match.
form.excludeHelp: Pictures with these tags are hidden. In the search this is a minus in front, e.g. “-hat”.
form.minScoreHelp: How well others rated the picture. Higher = only popular pictures, but fewer results. 50 is already fairly popular.
form.minSizeHelp: Smallest picture size in pixels. For wallpapers on a Full HD screen: 1920 × 1080.
form.orderHelp: “Newest first” is fastest and can page as far as you like. Other orders hit the page limit sooner without an account.
form.extra: Other search commands that are only in the text field: {{syntax}}

results.localOnly_one: Your account allows only {{count}} tag per search. We check these tags ourselves: {{tags}} – that takes longer, because more posts have to be looked through.
results.localOnly_other: Your account allows only {{count}} tags per search. We check these tags ourselves: {{tags}} – that takes longer, because more posts have to be looked through.
results.estimate_one: About {{count}} post will be looked through.
results.estimate_other: About {{count}} posts will be looked through.
results.none: Nothing on this page matches. Try “Load more” or change the search.
results.pageLimit: Without an account you can't page further. Sort by “Newest first” – then it goes as far as you like by post ID.

hidden.unavailable_one: {{count}} without a file (deleted or account only)
hidden.unavailable_other: {{count}} without a file (deleted or account only)

download.title: Download
download.limitHelp: Protects you from loading tens of thousands of files by accident. 100 is a good start.
download.limitMany: That's a lot of files – it can take long and need a lot of space.
download.speedHelp: How fast Conbert asks the site. Slower is kinder to the site and your account – the download keeps running in the background, even if you close the browser.
download.nightHelp: The download pauses automatically during the day and goes on at night – keeping your network and the site free in the daytime.
download.sampleHelp: Loads the reduced version (“sample”) instead of the original – saves a lot of space, but isn't as sharp.
download.destinationHelp: Where the pictures go: into your conversion list (to process them further) and/or straight to a storage location like your NAS.
download.started: The download is running – you see it in the list below.

naming.help: Placeholders in curly braces are replaced: {site} site, {id} post number, {md5} checksum, {artist}, {character}, {copyright} series, {rating}, {width}, {height}, {score}, {date}, {search_tags} your search, {ext} file extension.

settings.title: Booru
settings.intro: Age levels, own blacklist, file names, accounts and your own booru sites.

protect.title: Protect
protect.intro: Encrypt files so that only the right people can open them.

identify.title: What is this file really?
identify.teaser: The extension can lie, the first bytes can't. Hocus pocus – disguise blown!
identify.how: Almost every file format starts with a fixed mark, the “magic bytes”. A PNG always starts with 89 50 4E 47 (“‰PNG”), a PDF with “%PDF”, a ZIP with “PK”. The extension in the file name is just a label anyone can change. Conbert reads the first bytes and compares them with a list of known marks. Text has no such mark – it is recognised by containing only readable characters.

hex.title: Hex view
hex.teaser: See every single byte – explained in colour, even for huge files.
hex.how: A file is just a long row of bytes, numbers from 0 to 255. The hex view shows each byte as a two-digit hexadecimal number (00 to FF), with the same byte as a character on the right. For known formats Conbert reads the structure too and colours the parts: mark, header, blocks, the actual data and the end. Only the part you are looking at is loaded – that's why it works with several gigabytes too.

hashes.title: Checksums
hashes.teaser: A fingerprint for your file: did the download arrive intact?
hashes.how: A checksum (hash) is computed from all bytes of the file. If even a single bit changes, a completely different checksum comes out. Many download pages list the SHA-256 sum of their files. Paste it below: if it fits, your file is bit for bit the same as the original. Conbert computes all methods in a single pass over the file.

entropy.title: File entropy
entropy.teaser: How “random” are the bytes? Shows where pictures, text and encrypted data sit.
entropy.how: Entropy measures how evenly the 256 possible byte values occur – from 0 (always the same byte) to 8 bits per byte (all values equally often, like rolling dice). Text is usually around 4 to 5 because some letters are much more common. Compressed and encrypted data is close to 8. The chart shows the value piece by piece across the whole file.

detective.title: Detective scan
detective.teaser: Searches any file for hidden things – and gets them out. Elementary, my dear Watson!
detective.how: The scan reads the whole file and looks for the marks of known formats at every single position – like the tool “binwalk”. If “PK” or “%PDF” suddenly shows up in the middle of a picture, another file probably sits there. It also checks whether data hangs behind the actual end of the file, reads text notes in pictures and finds invisible characters in texts. You can download everything it finds; archives can be unpacked right away.

vault.title: Encrypt for …
vault.teaser: A lock only chosen people have the key to. Open sesame – but only for you!
vault.how: Conbert uses the open format “age”. Every file gets a random key the content is encrypted with (ChaCha20-Poly1305). This file key is then wrapped for each recipient with their public key (X25519) – or with a password (scrypt). Only someone with the matching private key or the password can open it. Everything happens in your browser; the files end up with you as .age files and the program “age” opens them too.

privacy.title: What does my file give away?
privacy.teaser: Where a photo was taken, with which camera, who wrote the document – check before you share it.
privacy.how: Files carry invisible extra info: photos often store the GPS location, the camera with its serial number, the time and a small preview. Word, Excel and PowerPoint remember authors, company, comments, changes and hidden content. Conbert reads all of it on your device (with ExifTool and a look into the Office file, which is a ZIP of text files inside) and sorts it by how much it tells about you. One click removes the metadata.

repair.title: File repair
repair.teaser: Broken checksums, cut-off pictures, wrong extension – Reparo!
repair.how: Many “broken” files are damaged in one small place only: a PNG checks every block with a checksum – if it doesn't fit, some programs refuse the whole picture. An interrupted download cuts off the end, then the closing mark is missing. Conbert recalculates wrong checksums, closes cut-off PNG, JPEG and GIF pictures properly, cuts off data behind the end if you like and fixes the extension. What's missing can't be conjured up – the missing part of a cut-off picture stays grey or empty.

ela.title: Forgery detector
ela.teaser: Was something retouched in here? Error level analysis makes edits visible.
ela.how: JPEG saves pictures lossily: every save loses a bit of detail, a lot the first time, less and less later on. Conbert saves your picture as JPEG once more and shows the difference to the original, amplified (error level analysis). An unedited photo looks similar everywhere. If a part was added or edited later, it was saved more often or differently – and glows differently from its surroundings. Everything runs in your browser.

treasure.title: Treasure map
treasure.teaser: Tear a secret into parts – it only reappears when enough of them come together.
treasure.how: Conbert splits your secret into several parts with “Shamir's secret sharing”, for example 5. You decide how many of them are needed to put it back together, for example 3. Any 3 parts bring the secret back – 2 parts tell nothing about it, not even a single letter. This is maths, not hide-and-seek: each part is a point on a random curve, and only enough points pin the curve down. Handy for the master password of your password manager: give one part each to family and friends, put one in a safe – if you lose one, nothing is lost, and no one alone gets to your secret. Everything happens in your browser.

ciphers.title: Secret writing
ciphers.teaser: Caesar, Vigenère, Morse, Braille & co. – write, play and crack them like a detective.
ciphers.how: These are the secret scripts from history books and adventure novels. Caesar moves every letter a few places along the alphabet, Vigenère by a different number each time, taken from a key word. Morse and Braille aren't encryption at all, just another way of writing – for radio and light, or for reading by touch. For every method Conbert shows how to crack it: mostly by counting how often each letter appears. For playing and learning – for real secrets use the key vault.

stego.title: Steganography
stego.teaser: Hide a secret message invisibly in the pixels of a picture – and conjure it up again.
stego.how: Every pixel is made of three colour values (red, green, blue) from 0 to 255. Nobody can see whether a value is 200 or 201. Conbert uses exactly this last, least important bit of every colour value (the “least significant bit”, LSB) and writes your message into it – 8 colour values make one character. Before that the message is packed and, if you set a password, encrypted with AES-256. The picture looks exactly as before. It is saved as PNG (or BMP) because both are lossless: a JPEG would smooth away the tiny differences when saving and destroy the message. Everything happens in your browser.

invisible.title: Invisible text
invisible.teaser: Tuck a message invisibly into an ordinary sentence – and track down hidden characters in copied text.
invisible.how: Unicode, the character table every computer uses, has characters with no width: they are there, but you can't see them – not in a chat, not in an editor. Conbert uses four of them like the digits 0 to 3 and writes your message with them after the first word of your text. Before that it is packed and, if you set a password, encrypted with AES-256. Every character of your message adds about four invisible ones. The other way round, Conbert finds such characters in any text you paste: hidden messages, markers some sites use to recognise copied text, or secret instructions for AI chatbots. Everything happens in your browser.

audiostego.title: Audio steganography
audiostego.teaser: Hide a secret message or file inaudibly in a piece of music – and get it back out.
audiostego.how: A piece of music is made of tens of thousands of measurements per second, the “samples”. On a CD that's 44,100 per second and channel, each a number between −32,768 and 32,767. Whether a number is 1,200 or 1,201 no one can hear – the difference is about as loud as a whisper next to a jackhammer. Conbert writes your message into exactly this last bit of every sample, packed first and AES-256 encrypted with a password. One minute of stereo music holds about 650 KB that way. It is saved as WAV or FLAC: both are lossless. MP3, AAC or Ogg would compute the tiny differences away when saving. Other formats are converted in your browser first.

spectrogram.title: Picture in the spectrogram
spectrogram.teaser: Turn a picture into sounds that show it again in a spectrogram – and look at any sound file as a spectrogram.
spectrogram.how: A spectrogram is a picture of sound: time runs from left to right, low tones are at the bottom, high ones at the top, and the brighter a spot, the louder that tone is at that moment. Conbert turns this round: every row of your picture becomes a tone of its own – high at the top, low at the bottom – and the brightness decides how loud it is right now. All tones together sound like shrill noise, but in a spectrogram (e.g. in Audacity or here in the second tab) your picture appears. Musicians like Aphex Twin hid faces in their songs this way. Everything happens in your browser.

metasecret.title: Secret message in metadata
metasecret.teaser: Write a message into the comment fields of a photo, PDF or song – and read such fields.
metasecret.how: Besides its content, almost every file carries a small note with details: camera, date, title, artist – the metadata. This includes comment fields that hardly any program shows. Conbert writes your message into such a field: for photos into the EXIF user comment, for PNG and GIF into the picture comment, for PDFs into the “Subject” field, for music and videos into the comment. The picture, document and sound stay unchanged. The message isn't invisible, though: anyone who opens the file properties can find it. With a password it only shows gibberish (AES-256). Everything happens in your browser.

ascii.title: ASCII art
ascii.teaser: Your picture drawn with nothing but letters and symbols – as text, web page or image.
ascii.how: Conbert lays a grid over your picture and measures how bright each cell is. Dark cells get “heavy” characters like @ or #, bright cells light ones like . or a space. Letters are about twice as tall as wide, so each cell is twice as tall too. With “In colour”, each character also gets the colour of its cell.

pixelart.title: Pixel art
pixelart.teaser: Turn a photo into a picture like on the Game Boy, NES or C64.
pixelart.how: Old consoles had few, big pixels and only a handful of colours. Conbert shrinks your picture to the chosen width and replaces every colour with the closest colour of the retro palette. Dithering fakes missing shades with a pattern of two colours – just like back then. For saving, every small pixel is blown up again into a sharp block.

glitch.title: Glitch art
glitch.teaser: Broken, but beautiful: glitches like in a damaged file – on purpose.
glitch.how: A JPEG doesn’t store the picture pixel by pixel but as a compressed data stream. Conbert changes a few random bytes in it (“datamoshing”). The file’s header stays intact, so it still opens – but from the broken spot on, the image viewer keeps calculating with wrong values: stripes, shifted blocks and strange colours appear. If a result doesn’t open at all, Conbert automatically tries another spot. Pictures in other formats are turned into JPEG first.

deepfry.title: Deep fry & JPEG death
deepfry.teaser: Meme look with screaming colours – and a picture saved so often that it falls apart.
deepfry.how: “Deep fry” pushes colours, contrast and noise far beyond reason. Then Conbert saves the picture again and again as a bad JPEG. Every save costs a little quality. To make the errors add up, the picture shifts by one pixel each time – so JPEG’s 8×8 blocks never line up again. At strength 0, only the “JPEG death” remains.

qr.title: QR codes
qr.teaser: Make QR codes for links, WLAN access or contacts – with a logo if you like – and read codes from pictures.
qr.how: A QR code stores text as a pattern of black and white squares. Part of it is error correction: even if a piece is missing or covered, the content can still be read. That is exactly what the logo in the middle relies on – with a logo, Conbert picks the strongest error correction (up to 30 % may be missing). WLAN and contacts have fixed formats that phones recognise, offering “Join network” or “Save contact”. Every finished code is read back once as a test. Everything happens on your device.

favicon.title: Icon & favicon generator
favicon.teaser: One picture in, every icon out: favicon.ico, app icons for iPhone and Android, a macOS icon and the manifest.
favicon.how: Browsers, phones and operating systems want icons in many sizes and formats. Conbert scales your picture to every size needed (big pictures step by step, so even 16 × 16 stays sharp) and packs them into the right files: favicon.ico for browser tabs, PNGs for iPhone and Android, an ICNS for macOS and a site.webmanifest so the site can go on the home screen with its icon. The lines for your web page’s <head> come with it. Everything happens on your device.

encode.title: Encode & decode
encode.teaser: Base64, hex, URL encoding and data URIs – for text and whole files, both ways.
encode.how: Some places only take plain text – emails, JSON, web addresses. Encodings rewrite any data so it fits there: Base64 uses 64 harmless characters (the file grows by about a third), hex writes every byte as two digits 0–9/a–f, URL encoding replaces special characters with %-codes. A data URI is Base64 with the file type in front and can be used directly as a picture address in HTML or CSS. This is no encryption: anyone can turn it back.

archiveimage.title: Archive in a picture
archiveimage.teaser: Hide your secret files as a stowaway in a harmless picture.
archiveimage.how: Pictures often ignore extra data that is simply added to the end of the file. This trick takes your ZIP, RAR or 7Z archive and invisibly sticks it behind the picture data. A normal click still shows the picture, but an unpacking program finds the hidden archive.

polyglot.title: Polyglot files
polyglot.teaser: Two files in one: a picture or PDF and a ZIP archive merge seamlessly.
polyglot.how: Instead of just tacking the ZIP onto the end, it is built right into the structure of the host file – for example as a specially marked extra block in a PNG or as an inconspicuous addition to a PDF. Both files stay completely intact and can be read without errors.

split.title: File splitter
split.teaser: Cut a big file into parts – and put parts back together.
split.how: Many messengers, e-mail programs and upload pages only take files up to a certain size. Conbert cuts your file into pieces of the same size and adds a number to the name (film.mp4.001, film.mp4.002 …). The content stays exactly the same. To join them, drop all parts here under “Join” – or open the first part with 7-Zip. Everything happens on your device; the file is not uploaded.

emojimosaic.title: Emoji mosaic
emojimosaic.teaser: Rebuild your photo from emojis – as a picture or as text to send.
emojimosaic.how: Conbert splits your picture into small squares and works out the average colour of each. Then it looks for the emoji whose colour fits best and puts it there. Every device has its own emoji pictures, so Conbert measures the emoji colours right on your device. As text, the mosaic therefore looks a little different on another phone.

ringtone.title: Ringtone maker
ringtone.teaser: Cut your favourite part out of a song – with a soft start and end.
ringtone.how: You pick a part of your song (at most 40 seconds – iPhones take no more). Conbert lets the start fade in and the end fade out, so the ringtone does not stop abruptly. If you like, it is made as loud as possible without distortion. Finally it is saved as MP3 (for most phones) or M4R (for iPhones). Everything happens on your device.

testfiles.title: Test files
testfiles.teaser: Make files of exactly the size you need – or a test picture, test tone, test PDF and test video.
testfiles.how: Sometimes you just need a file to try something out: does the upload work up to 100 MB? Does a 2 GB movie really arrive on the NAS? Does the TV play 1080p videos? Conbert makes such files right on your device, nothing is uploaded. Files of a fixed size are filled with zeros, random data or lines of text. Random data can't be compressed, so you test real transfers without a ZIP or the server making them smaller. Your browser encodes the test video itself (WebCodecs): colour bars, a running clock, the frame number and one beep per second – so you see right away whether picture and sound stay in sync.

compare.title: Compare
compare.teaser: Put two files side by side and see exactly what is different.
compare.how: First Conbert compares the two files byte by byte – every single character of the raw data. If all are the same, the files are identical, whatever their names. If they differ, Conbert looks closer. For text it finds (like the “diff” program) the smallest number of lines to delete and add to turn file A into file B. For pictures it compares every pixel and colours changed spots red; a tolerance hides tiny JPEG noise. For all other files you see where (offset) which bytes are different. Everything happens on your device.

identify.match: All genuine: name and content agree – “{{format}}”.
identify.matchHint: Extension and content agree. Programs open the file the way they should.
identify.mismatch: In disguise! The name says “{{claimed}}”, but inside is “{{real}}”.

identify.textMismatchHint: Common cause: the download delivered an error page or a redirect instead of the file. Open the hex view to read the text – it often says what went wrong.
