msg.saving to a storage location failed: Saving to a storage location failed
msg.sync with the storage location failed: Sync with the storage location failed

archiveKeep.label: Keep the server archive for
archiveKeep.help: How long downloads without a storage location stay on the server before Conbert deletes them by itself. Applies to new downloads; they count against the user’s storage quota. Longer = more convenient, but needs more disk space.

quota.title: Storage on the server
quota.help: What of yours is on the server right now: uploaded files, finished results and downloads to pick up. Conbert cleans this up by itself after a while. The admin sets the limit.

helpCenter.title: Help
helpCenter.intro: Here you'll find explanations for every area, answers to common questions and a dictionary of technical terms.

start.body: Drop a file on the start page, pick a target format and click “Convert”. That's all you need to know – everything else is optional.
start.modes: You choose where the conversion happens: 🖥 on this device (most private), ☁ on the server (faster, more formats) or ✨ automatic.
start.expert: The “Expert” switch at the top right shows more settings. Without it you only see what matters most.

engines.body: Conbert uses many specialised programs – for example one for photos, one for videos and one for documents. You can see which ones exist and whether they're ready in the settings.

helpCenter.glossaryEmpty: No term found. Try a shorter word.

convert.title: Convert
convert.body: Turn a file into another format, for example an iPhone photo (HEIC) into a JPG or a Word document into a PDF. You can drop many files at once. Tip: under “What do you want to do?” just pick the purpose (e.g. “For WhatsApp”) and Conbert sets everything up for you.

compress.title: Compress
compress.body: Make a file smaller without changing its format. Pick “Balanced” if you're unsure. If the file would get bigger, Conbert keeps the original. For photos, location and camera data are removed by default too.

download.title: Download
download.body: Paste a link from YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Reddit and others. Conbert first shows you what it found, then saves it to your server. Some sites need cookies for private or age-restricted content.

booru.title: Booru
booru.body: Download pictures from image boards such as Gelbooru or Safebooru – one by link, or all pictures for certain keywords (tags). A block list filters out content you don't want to see.

subscriptions.title: Subscriptions
subscriptions.body: Follow profiles or keywords. Conbert checks for new posts regularly and downloads them for you.

swipe.title: Swipe
swipe.body: Sort downloaded pictures quickly: swipe right to keep, left to throw out. Handy when a subscription has loaded a lot of pictures.

workflows.title: Workflows
workflows.body: A workflow is a chain of steps that run automatically one after another – for example “download → convert to MP4 → shrink → save on the NAS”. Best start with a template.

pdf.title: PDF
pdf.body: Merge PDFs, split them, rotate or reorder pages and make scanned PDFs searchable (text recognition).

workshop.title: Workshop
workshop.body: Playful file tricks: find out what a file really is, hide a message in a picture or paint a picture into a sound. Everything runs on your device.

archive.title: Archive
archive.body: Your finished results and history live here. You can download files again or repeat a conversion with the same settings.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Choose where conversions run by default, connect storage locations (NAS, Nextcloud …), add cookies for the downloader and switch the language.

admin.title: Administration
admin.body: For admins only: create more accounts, reset passwords, set storage quotas and see how busy the server is. Under “Groups” you decide who may use which functions, and under “Sign-in through LDAP” you connect Conbert to your user directory. The “Log” shows what happened on the server – you choose there how detailed it is.

whichFormat.a: JPG or WebP for photos, PNG for pictures with a see-through background, MP4 for videos, MP3 for music, PDF for documents you pass on. The format menu says what each format is good for – and ⭐ marks the recommendation.

whyBigger.q: Why did my file get bigger?
whyBigger.a: Some formats pack less tightly. A JPG photo saved as PNG often becomes three to five times bigger, because PNG leaves nothing out. If you want to save space, use “Compress” or a format such as WebP.

whyStutter.a: Usually the frame rate (pictures per second) is too low, or the bitrate is too tight for a lot of movement. Keep the frame rate at “same as original” and choose a higher quality. If it only stutters on an old device, pick a smaller resolution (e.g. 720p).

mp4VsMkv.q: What's the difference between MP4 and MKV?
mp4VsMkv.a: Both are “boxes” for video, sound and subtitles. MP4 plays almost everywhere (phone, TV, browser). MKV can do more (several audio tracks, many subtitles) but doesn't play on every device. When in doubt: MP4.

localOrServer.q: Should I convert on this device or on the server?
localOrServer.a: “On this device” is the most private – the file never leaves your computer. “On the server” is faster and supports more formats. If you're unsure, keep “Automatic”.

localNotWorking.q: Why doesn't “On this device” work for me?
localNotWorking.a: Some tools need a secure connection. If you open Conbert via an address like http://192.168.1.20:3313, the browser blocks them. Fix: open Conbert over HTTPS (for example with a reverse proxy) or directly on the server via http://localhost:3313. Until then, Conbert converts those files on the server.

transparencyLost.q: Why is the see-through background white now?
transparencyLost.a: Not every format can store transparency. JPG can't and fills those areas with white. Use PNG, WebP or AVIF if the background should stay see-through.

whereAreFiles.q: Where do my files go and how long do they stay?
whereAreFiles.a: When converting on this device they only stay in your browser. On the server they sit in a separate folder per job and are deleted automatically after a short time (1 hour by default). Whatever you save to a storage location stays there.

whyCookies.q: Why does the downloader need cookies?
whyCookies.a: Cookies are small files a website uses to recognise you. For private profiles, stories or age-restricted videos, Conbert has to act as if you were signed in. To do that, export your cookies from the browser and upload them in the settings. The guide “Export cookies” shows how.

forgotPassword.q: I forgot my password. What now?
forgotPassword.a: Ask an admin to reset your password under “Administration”. If you are the only admin yourself, see the section “Forgot the admin password” in the installation guide.

installApp.q: Can I install Conbert like an app?
installApp.a: Yes. In the browser menu choose “Install app” or “Add to home screen”. On a phone you can then send links straight via “Share → Conbert”, and converting on your device also works without internet. This only works over HTTPS or localhost.

quotaFull.a: Your admin decided how much space you may use on the server. Delete old results in the archive or ask the admin for more space.

missingArea.q: Why is an area missing for me, for example “Download”?
missingArea.a: Your administrator can switch functions off for single people or groups. Blocked areas then disappear from the navigation. If you need an area, ask your administrator to unlock it for you.

archive.text: A file that packs many other files together – like a moving box. Often also made smaller so it's quicker to send.

bitrate.text: How much data per second is stored in a video or song. More bitrate = better quality but a bigger file. Example: music sounds good at 192 kbit/s, a normal video looks good at 4–8 Mbit/s.

codec.text: The method used to squeeze picture or sound, for example H.264 for video or AAC for sound. A player has to know the codec, otherwise the screen stays black or silent.

compression.text: Making a file smaller. Either without loss (like folding clothes neatly) or with loss (like leaving out unimportant details).

container.text: The “box” of a video, e.g. MP4 or MKV. It holds picture, sound and subtitles, each stored with its own codec. That's why one MP4 file plays on a device and another doesn't.

cookie.text: A small file a website uses to remember that you're signed in. Treat exported cookies like a password.

dpi.text: “Dots per inch” – how fine a picture is when printed. 300 DPI is good for photos on paper; for screens the value hardly matters.

exif.text: Extra information in photos: camera, time taken and often the exact location (GPS). Better remove it before sharing.

framerate.text: How many single pictures a video shows per second. 24–30 is normal, 60 looks especially smooth, below 20 it stutters.

hash.text: A “fingerprint” of a file, e.g. SHA-256. If even one byte changes, the fingerprint is completely different. It's used to check that a file is unchanged.

https.text: An encrypted connection to a website (the padlock in the browser). Some Conbert features, such as converting on your device or installing as an app, only work with it or via localhost.

lossless.text: Nothing gets lost when saving – the picture or sound is just as good as before. Examples: PNG, FLAC, ZIP.

lossy.text: Saving leaves out details you hardly notice – in return the file gets much smaller. Examples: JPG, MP3, MP4. Saving again and again lowers the quality a little each time.

magicBytes.text: The first bytes of a file that reveal its real format – no matter what extension it has. A PNG, for example, always starts with “‰PNG”.

metadata.text: Information about a file that isn't the content itself: title, artist, author, date taken, camera, location.

nas.text: A small computer with hard drives on your home network where the whole family can store files (e.g. from Synology or QNAP).

ocr.text: A program reads the text out of a picture or scan. Afterwards you can search the PDF and copy text.

polygon.text: A small surface (usually a triangle) that 3D models are made of. More polygons = a finer shape but a bigger file.

resolution.text: How many pixels a picture or video has, e.g. 1920 × 1080 (Full HD). More pixels = sharper but bigger.

reverseProxy.text: A program (e.g. Caddy, Nginx Proxy Manager, Traefik) that sits in front of Conbert, handles HTTPS encryption and, if you like, sign-in too.

sampleRate.text: How often per second a sound is measured, e.g. 44,100 Hz (CD quality). More isn't needed for normal listening.

smb.text: The usual way Windows, Macs and NAS devices share folders on a home network. The address looks like \\nas\Photos or smb://nas/Photos.

steganography.text: Hiding a message in a picture or sound so nobody notices. The picture looks completely normal afterwards.

texture.text: A picture “glued” onto the surface of a 3D model so it looks like wood or fabric, for example.

transparency.text: See-through areas in a picture, e.g. a logo without background. PNG, WebP and GIF support it, JPG doesn't.

vector.text: A picture made of lines and shapes instead of dots (e.g. SVG). It stays sharp at any size – ideal for logos and icons.

wasm.text: A technique that lets real programs run right inside the browser. That's how Conbert converts files on your device without uploading them.

workflow.text: A fixed sequence of steps that Conbert runs automatically, e.g. “convert, shrink, save”.

ldap.text: A central directory of user accounts, passwords and groups – for example Active Directory in companies or lldap at home. Instead of an own account for every program, everyone signs in with the same account.

userGroup.text: Several accounts that get the same permissions together. Example: the group “Family” may download videos, everyone else may not. That way the admin doesn't have to set up every person on their own.

log.text: The server's diary: every line records what happened when – for example “Download failed” with the reason. Helps to find problems. The admin decides how detailed it is.

purposes.movedToCompress_other: {{count}} files are now under “Compress”, because size is what matters most here.

messenger.label: Send via WhatsApp / messenger
messenger.summary: Small files that open on every phone.

why.image: Every phone opens JPG. Quality 80 looks like the original on a phone screen but is much smaller – and the location is removed.
why.video: Every phone plays MP4. 720p is enough for a small screen and keeps the file small enough for messengers.
why.audio: Every phone plays MP3, and it's small enough to send.
why.document: A PDF looks the same on every phone, even without an Office app.

email.label: Send by e-mail (under 10 MB)
email.summary: Made small enough to go through as an attachment.

why.image: Many e-mail providers refuse attachments over 10 MB. So the picture becomes a JPG of just under 10 MB or less.
why.video: Many e-mail providers refuse attachments over 10 MB. So the video becomes an MP4 that stays just below that. For long videos the quality drops noticeably.
why.audio: Many e-mail providers refuse attachments over 10 MB. So the sound becomes an MP3 that stays just below that.
why.pdf: Many e-mail providers refuse attachments over 10 MB. So Conbert tries the levels from best quality to “Smallest” and takes the best one that stays below. An exact size isn’t possible for PDFs.
why.document: Anyone can open a PDF and it looks the same everywhere – even without Word.

why.image: WebP is much smaller than JPG or PNG, supports transparency and works in every current browser. So the page loads faster.
why.video: MP4 plays in every browser. 1080p is sharp enough for almost any website.
why.document: HTML is the format of websites – the text can be used directly.
why.font: WOFF2 is the smallest font format and every browser supports it.
why.model: GLB is the standard format for 3D in the browser. Compression makes it much smaller so it loads quickly.

why.image: A PDF prints at the right size on any printer and at any print shop. The quality stays high.
why.vector: In a PDF the graphic stays perfectly sharp at any size.
why.document: A PDF prints exactly as it looks on screen, everywhere.

phone.label: Play on iPhone/Android
phone.summary: Formats every phone opens without an extra app.

why.image: Every phone opens JPG – unlike HEIC, which many Android phones can't show.
why.video: MP4 with H.264 plays on every iPhone and Android phone without an extra app.
why.audio: M4A (AAC) sounds better than MP3 at the same size and plays on iPhone and Android.
why.ebook: Apple Books, Google Play Books and almost every reading app open EPUB.

why.model: Every slicer (Cura, PrusaSlicer, Bambu Studio …) reads STL. Colours and textures are lost – printing doesn't need them.

gameEngine.label: For game engines / web 3D
gameEngine.summary: Compact GLB for Unity, Godot, three.js and others.

why.model: GLB is a single file with model and textures that Godot, Unity, Unreal and three.js read directly. Compression and textures up to 2048 pixels keep it small.

why.all: The file keeps its format and is compressed in a balanced way: much smaller, with no visible difference.

welcome.title: Welcome to Conbert!
welcome.body: Conbert converts files and makes them smaller – photos, videos, music, documents, 3D models and more. This short tour shows you the essentials. You can end it at any time.

purpose.title: Just say what it's for
purpose.body: Not sure which format you need? Pick the purpose here, for example “Send via WhatsApp” – Conbert sets everything up and tells you why.

dropzone.title: Drop files here
dropzone.body: Drag files or whole folders here, click to choose them, or paste them with Ctrl+V. Every file gets a card with a preview and a target format.

modes.title: On this device or on the server?
modes.body: 🖥 On this device your files stay private on your computer. ☁ On the server it's faster and there are more formats. ✨ Automatic lets Conbert decide for you – that's the default.

nav.title: Even more tools
nav.body: Up here you switch to Compress, downloading videos, PDF tools, the workshop with file tricks and your archive.

expert.title: More settings
expert.body: Normally you only see what matters most. “Expert” shows every setting, such as bitrate or resolution.

help.title: Help when you need it
help.body: Here you'll find explanations for every area, common questions and a dictionary of technical terms. You can also restart the tour there. And next to every setting, the ⓘ explains what it does.

offline.title: No connection to the server
offline.body: You can keep working: converting and compressing on this device also work offline – with every tool that was loaded before. Signing in, downloading and everything the server does only work again with a connection.

blender.title: Blender
blender.help: Blender is a free 3D program. Conbert uses it for formats nothing else opens: Blender files (.blend), USD and Alembic. Because Blender is very large, it isn't part of the container – you download it here once. It stays installed when Conbert is updated.
blender.intro: For .blend, USD and Alembic files. Only downloaded when you install it here.
blender.unsupported: There is no official Blender for this device: Blender only offers Linux versions for regular PCs and servers (x64), not for ARM devices such as a Raspberry Pi or many NAS.
blender.installed: Installed – Blender files, USD and Alembic can be converted now.
blender.source: Source: download.blender.org (official release, the checksum is verified). Stored in /data/tools/blender.

blocked.title: This function is blocked for you
blocked.body: Your administrator switched this area off for your account. If you need it, ask them.

permissions.serverConvertOff: Your administrator switched off converting on the server for you, so your files are always converted on this device.
permissions.onlyHidden: This function runs entirely in your browser, so Conbert can only hide it – someone who knows their way around could still open it.

convert.name: Convert & compress
convert.help: The start page for converting and the “Compress” page. When it's off, the person doesn't see these pages.

serverConvert.name: Convert on the server
serverConvert.help: Send files to the server to convert them (faster, more formats). When it's off, files are only converted on the person's own device – that costs the server no computing time.

downloader.name: Download (videos & pictures)
downloader.help: Download videos and pictures from sites like YouTube or Instagram, including subscriptions to profiles and channels.

booru.name: Booru
booru.help: Download pictures from booru sites, search by tags and booru subscriptions.

workflows.name: Workflows
workflows.help: Create and start own processing chains, including “Then automatically …” after downloads.

storage.name: Storage locations
storage.help: Set up own storage locations like a NAS, SMB shares or Nextcloud and save files there or open them from there.

media.name: Swipe & similar pictures
media.help: Swipe through pictures on a storage location, tidy up and find duplicate or similar pictures.

ai.name: AI tools
ai.help: Turn speech into text (Whisper), remove backgrounds and upscale pictures. These tools need a lot of computing time on the server.

workshop.name: Workshop
workshop.help: The FileWizard workshop with file tricks like “What is this file really?”, steganography or the file splitter.

pdf.name: PDF tools
pdf.help: Merge, split, sort and rotate PDFs.

apiTokens.name: API keys
apiTokens.help: Create own access keys for scripts and the command line. A key may never do more than the person themselves.

groups.title: Groups
groups.intro: Groups restrict who may use which functions of Conbert. Without a group, everyone may do everything.
groups.help: Everyone is automatically in “All users” – that group allows everything. Own groups restrict: whatever is switched off in a group is blocked for its members. If someone is in several groups, every block counts. In the user management you can also always allow or always block single functions per person – that wins. Administrators may always do everything.
groups.dialogIntro: Switch off what the members of this group shouldn't use, and choose who belongs to it.
groups.name: Name
groups.functionsHint: Switched on = allowed. Switched off = blocked and hidden for the members – even if another group allows it.
groups.grantsAdminHelp: For accounts from LDAP or the reverse proxy: whoever is in this group there automatically becomes an administrator when signing in – and loses it again after leaving the group. You still change local accounts by hand.
groups.proxyName: Group name at the reverse proxy (optional)
groups.proxyNameHint: For example “conbert-download”. Leave empty if you don't use a reverse proxy with groups.
groups.proxyNameHelp: If your reverse proxy (e.g. Authelia or Authentik) sends a person's groups along, everyone with this group name automatically joins this group.
groups.deleteWarning: The members lose the functions only this group allowed. Their accounts and files stay.

ldap.title: Sign-in through LDAP
ldap.intro: Let people sign in with their existing account from your directory – for example Active Directory, OpenLDAP or lldap.
ldap.help: LDAP is a directory where companies and many home servers keep their user accounts and groups in one place. Once set up here, Conbert checks user name and password with your directory. On the first sign-in the person automatically gets a Conbert account. Local Conbert accounts (e.g. your admin account) keep working – even when the directory can't be reached.

presets.label: Template
presets.hint: Fills in filters and attributes. You enter the address, account and search base yourself.

enabled.label: Switch on sign-in through LDAP
enabled.help: When it's on, people from your directory can sign in. Switching it off blocks new LDAP sign-ins – existing accounts stay in Conbert.

url.label: Server address
url.help: ldaps:// encrypts the connection from the start (usually port 636). With ldap:// (usually port 389) it is unencrypted – then switch on “StartTLS” below if your server supports it. lldap uses port 3890 by default.

startTls.label: Encrypt the connection with StartTLS
startTls.help: Only for ldap:// addresses: the connection starts unencrypted and is encrypted right away. Leave it off for ldaps://.

tlsVerify.label: Check the server's certificate
tlsVerify.help: Protects against another computer pretending to be your server. Only switch it off if your server has a self-signed certificate and you don't want to enter your own CA certificate.

bindDn.label: Service account (bind DN)
bindDn.help: Conbert uses this account to search the directory for users and groups. Best use an own read-only account. Leave empty if your server allows anonymous searching.

bindPassword.label: Password of the service account
bindPassword.hint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.

userBase.label: Search base for users
userBase.help: The folder in the directory below which the user accounts are. Conbert searches there and in all subfolders.

userFilter.label: User filter
userFilter.hint: {{username}} is replaced by the user name that was entered.
userFilter.help: Tells Conbert how to recognise a user account. The placeholder {{username}} must be in it. Example: (&(objectClass=person)(uid={{username}})). Only let certain people in? Add e.g. (memberOf=cn=conbert,ou=groups,dc=home) – or use “Only members of imported groups” below.

groupBase.label: Search base for groups (optional)
groupBase.hint: For example ou=groups,dc=home. Empty = same as for users.
groupBase.help: The folder below which your groups are. From there you can take groups over into Conbert.

usernameAttr.label: Attribute for the user name
usernameAttr.hint: uid for OpenLDAP/lldap, sAMAccountName for Active Directory.

groupFilter.label: Group filter
groupFilter.help: How Conbert recognises a group. Leave empty if you don't want to use groups from the directory.

memberAttr.label: How groups store their members
memberAttr.help: member: usual groups (groupOfNames, Active Directory). uniqueMember: groupOfUniqueNames. memberUid: Unix groups (posixGroup) that only store the user name. Nested groups (groups in groups) are not resolved.

caCert.label: Own CA certificate (optional)
caCert.help: Does your server have a certificate from an own certificate authority (e.g. from the company domain controller or your NAS)? Paste the root certificate in PEM format here (starts with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----). Then the check works without switching off “Check the server's certificate”.

onlyImportedGroups.label: Only members of imported groups may sign in
onlyImportedGroups.help: On: whoever is in none of the groups you took over from LDAP under “Groups” can't get in. That way you decide in the directory who may use Conbert. Someone who leaves a group is blocked at the next sync.

syncHours.label: Sync automatically every
syncHours.help: How often Conbert asks your directory who is in which group and who still exists. Every sign-in also syncs right away. 0 = only at sign-in and by button.

test.title: Test the connection
test.intro: Tries the settings above without saving them. Optionally enter an account to test a sign-in, too.
test.connected: Connection works: {{users}} users and {{groups}} groups found.

loginFailed.notFound: This user doesn't exist – or the user filter matches several accounts.
loginFailed.wrongPassword: The user was found, but the password is wrong.
loginFailed.notInGroup: The password is right, but the person is in no imported group and therefore may not sign in.

sync.done: Sync finished: {{users}} LDAP accounts checked, {{disabled}} blocked.

import.title: Take groups over from LDAP
import.intro: Choose the groups from your directory you want to use in Conbert. Their members are added automatically at every sign-in and sync. You decide afterwards which functions a group allows.
import.none: No groups found. Check the search base and group filter in the LDAP settings.
import.truncated: There are more groups than fit here – enter a search term.
import.done_one: {{count}} group taken over. Now choose which functions it allows.
import.done_other: {{count}} groups taken over. Now choose which functions they allow.

clearList.downloads: All finished, failed and cancelled downloads leave the list. Running and waiting ones stay. The files themselves stay at your storage locations and in the server archive.
clearList.booru: All finished, failed and cancelled searches leave the list. Running, waiting and paused ones stay. Pictures at your storage locations stay; pictures only waiting for the conversion list are deleted from the server.
